Required on-site stays: up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and March 2028 for installation, exhibition and deinstallation.
grants.amount: EUR 24,000 total package per winner: EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production budget, and up to EUR 3,000 for travel, accommodation and subsistence, plus a separate budget covering one month of housing in Ceske Budejovice. Two positions available. Free to apply.
grants.duration: January 2027 to April 2028, with on-site blocks in early 2027 and March 2028
grants.description: A fully funded art-science residency from Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice, European Capital of Culture 2028, exploring how art and science can collaborate on urgent environmental challenges: climate emergence, sustainable agriculture, geoengineering, permaculture, water resource management, and the broader ecological impacts on local communities. Selected residents work in direct collaboration with local scientists in Ceske Budejovice. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, designers, creatives and artist collectives with more than 5 years of professional creative practice and documented interdisciplinary work; experience in community engagement and science collaborations is essential; applicants must be 18+, of any nationality, and legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. WHAT YOU GET: a EUR 24,000 package (EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production, up to EUR 3,000 travel and subsistence) plus one month of housing covered separately; two winners are selected. STRUCTURE: the residency runs January 2027 to April 2028, with a required on-site stay of up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and a March 2028 stay for festival installation, exhibition and deinstallation. HOW TO APPLY: online form with project title, a written proposal of max 250 words, a scientific direction statement (max 100 words), artistic vision (max 100 words), community connection plan (max 100 words), a super short pitch (3 to 30 words), 3 to 7 images, an optional 1-minute video, a portfolio link and contact information. Two-round selection (online application then interview); winners notified by November 2026. Deadline 28 September 2026 at midnight CET.

grants.title: ESA Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP): rolling open call for ideas
grants.location: Ideas can be submitted from anywhere in the world via ideas.esa.int. To implement a funded idea yourself, you or your affiliated entity must be eligible to do business with ESA under its procurement regulations, which in practice means being based in an ESA member state (the Netherlands qualifies).
grants.amount: Varies by route and campaign. Successful ideas are supported through PhD or postdoctoral research co-funded by ESA and universities, early technology development activities, or system studies. Free to submit.
grants.duration: Rolling: open channels have no deadline; targeted campaigns are regularly issued with their own timelines
grants.description: OSIP is the European Space Agency's standing front door for unsolicited novel ideas, launched in 2019 and now the main entry point for new concepts into ESA, both in response to specific problems and through open calls. HOW IT WORKS: ideas are submitted through two mechanisms. Campaigns are targeted calls responding to specific questions with defined timelines (recent examples include Future Navigation Demonstrators and elements for the EOCognitiveLab mission); Channels are permanently open, open-ended calls on broader topics with no deadline. Submissions can go through an optional community discussion phase, with voting and comments, before expert evaluation by ESA. WHO CAN SUBMIT: individuals, businesses, universities and organisations anywhere in the world. The catch for funding: to implement a funded idea yourself, you must be eligible to do business with ESA under Article 18 of its procurement regulations, which in practice means affiliation with an entity in an ESA member state. WHAT FUNDING LOOKS LIKE: successful ideas are typically supported as co-funded PhD or postdoctoral research (ESA plus a university), early technology development activities, or system studies; amounts vary by route and campaign. WHY IT IS ON THE DESK: this is the one genuinely public, always-open route into ESA for independent researchers, technologists and artists working with space data or space technology concepts; new campaigns appear regularly, so checking the platform periodically is worthwhile. Submit via ideas.esa.int.

grants.title: Beinecke Library Short-Term Research Fellowships 2027-2028 (Yale)
grants.organization: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University
grants.location: Onsite at Yale Library Special Collections, New Haven, Connecticut, USA. Open to academic and independent scholars locally and globally, regardless of institutional association.
grants.amount: USD 5,000 per month for research visits between two weeks and two months. Funding is paid at the beginning of the fellowship where possible (payment to international fellows often takes several weeks); fellows are responsible for taxes on the award. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Two weeks to two months of onsite research, conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028; awards cannot be deferred
grants.description: The Beinecke Library Fellowship Program offers competitive short-term fellowships to support research projects that substantively engage with Yale Library Special Collections materials. WHO CAN APPLY: academic and independent scholars, locally and globally, with or without an institutional affiliation; the library explicitly welcomes applicants regardless of institutional association, race, cultural background, ability, sexual orientation, gender or socioeconomic status. Applications using traditional archival and bibliographic research methods are encouraged, and so are creative, interdisciplinary and non-traditional approaches to working with the collections, which makes this a live option for artists and writers whose practice is research-driven. WHAT YOU GET: USD 5,000 per month for an onsite research visit of between two weeks and two months, paid at the start of the fellowship whenever possible (international fellows should expect payment to take several weeks); fellows pay their own taxes on the award. TIMELINE: applications for the 2027-2028 awards opened 1 June 2026 and close 15 August 2026, via Interfolio; all decisions are notified by 31 January 2027; research must be conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, and awards cannot be deferred.

grants.title: KNOWCASE Open Call 2027: permanent digital-culture installation in Madrid (Sonar+D x Fundacion Cotec)
grants.location: Installation at the KNOWCASE storefront of Fundacion Cotec's headquarters in Chamberi, Madrid, Spain, a street-level venue visible 24/7. The call is international; applications accepted in Spanish, other official languages of Spain, or English.
grants.amount: Up to EUR 100,000 (plus VAT), all-inclusive: conceptualisation, design, technical development, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance.
grants.duration: Installation displayed for a minimum of 24 months, starting February 2027
grants.description: Fundacion Cotec (a Spanish innovation-focused non-profit) and Sonar+D, building on an initial experiment at Sonar 2026, invite proposals for a long-term installation at KNOWCASE, the street-level showcase of Cotec's Madrid headquarters in Chamberi, visible to the public 24 hours a day. THEME: digital culture, meaning projects that combine knowledge, research, science and data with art, technology and social impact. Cotec's stated priorities are the big transitions (analogue to digital, linear to circular economy, tangible to intangible) plus innovation ecosystems and R&D&I, the climate crisis, the future of work and learning, social divides, citizen participation and democratic health. WHAT YOU GET: a budget of up to EUR 100,000 plus VAT covering everything (design, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance), and a minimum 24-month public display from February 2027. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, collectives, designers, technologists, universities, research centres, startups, businesses, creative agencies, producers, cultural institutions and multidisciplinary teams, internationally; applicants must demonstrate solid experience and a relevant portfolio. CONSTRAINTS: the proposal must be original and never previously exhibited, must include participative or interactive elements, must encourage critical thinking, and must be technically and financially viable for the full 24+ month exhibition period (durability and maintenance are central selection criteria). Selection weighs conceptual quality highest (40 percent), followed by public interactivity (25 percent). HOW TO APPLY: one PDF of maximum 15 pages containing summary, concept, technical proposal, visuals, budget, timeline, team profile, portfolio and declaration, in Spanish, another official language of Spain, or English, via the application portal linked from the terms and conditions. Results announced 14 October 2026. Deadline 7 September 2026 at midnight CEST.

grants.title: Project Tech4Dev: AI Cohort Program 3.0 (NGOs building AI solutions)
grants.location: Remote cohort programme. No geographic restriction is stated in the call, but the framing is India-centred: preference goes to problems involving multi-modal input and Indic languages.
grants.amount: FLAG, UNVERIFIED: no grant amount, stipend, fee or compute credit is stated. What the call describes is hands-on implementation support, mentorship and expert guidance across three sprints; participating NGOs must invest one person's full bandwidth for the duration.
grants.duration: Six months, tentatively mid-September 2026 to January or February 2027 (subject to change)
grants.description: The third round of Project Tech4Dev's AI Cohort, a hands-on implementation programme for NGOs designing, building and deploying responsible AI solutions inside their own programmes. Cohort 2.0 worked with seven NGOs across education, civic engagement, youth development and nonprofit technology, who built and piloted AI teaching assistants, volunteer coaches, mentoring tools and decision-support systems; the organisers' stated lesson was that adoption turns on understanding user needs, testing rapidly, measuring impact and building responsibly rather than on the technology itself. Cohort 3.0 is aimed at organisations ready to move past exploration into solutions that can be deployed in real-world settings. STRUCTURE (three sprints over roughly six months): Discovery Sprint (months 1 to 2) covering problem discovery, use-case prioritisation, data-readiness assessment, user research and solution design; Build Sprint (months 2 to 5) covering prototype development, implementation sprints, user testing, mentorship and responsible AI evaluations; and Activation Sprint (month 6) covering pilot deployment, impact assessment, operationalisation planning and a final showcase with peers and ecosystem partners. SELECTION CRITERIA: NGOs must show some in-house technical or data capability, ideally a dedicated person who can anchor the work (not necessarily an AI expert, but able to manage workflows, communicate operational requirements and work with mentors and experts); must commit one person's full bandwidth for the whole programme, including aligning leadership, adapting operations and making room to test, monitor and refine; and preference goes to problems involving multi-modal input, especially Indic languages, and to use cases built on LLMs. Applications are open to nonprofits across sectors, with priority to climate-focused organisations whose AI use cases could improve programme delivery, decision-making or community outcomes. Apply via the Google Form linked from the announcement before 10 August 2026.

grants.title: Collider: Program Manager (AI safety fieldbuilding, New York)
grants.location: Hybrid in New York City, USA. No visa sponsorship: candidates must already have the right to work in the US.
grants.amount: USD 150,000 to 180,000 base salary, plus health insurance, 401(k) and 20 days paid time off. The one-day in-person work trial is paid.
grants.duration: Full-time, permanent; start date flexible
grants.description: Collider, the New York coworking and convening space for AI safety and other high-impact work, is hiring a Program Manager to design, run and scale the programmes that grow the AI safety talent pipeline and infrastructure in New York. The role owns programmes end to end, from concept to launch to iteration, working with researchers, practitioners, educators, funders and partner organisations. WHAT YOU DO: design and operate fieldbuilding programmes (fellowships, training programmes, workshops, conferences, cohort courses and new formats); own budget, timeline, vendor relationships, participant experience and post-programme evaluation; recruit and coordinate mentors, instructors, advisors and participants, and build the pipelines and selection processes that hold quality as things scale; define and track outcomes with metrics beyond participant satisfaction, and iterate on the evidence; maintain relationships across research labs, university groups, training programmes (MATS, ARENA, BlueDot, SPAR, AI Safety Camp are named), grantmakers and adjacent communities; represent Collider externally; write programme reports, strategy memos, post-mortems and public materials; and work with leadership on which programmes to launch, scale or sunset. REQUIRED: 3+ years of programme or project management, ideally running cohort, fellowship or training programmes; substantive understanding of the AI safety field, its organisations, its main research agendas (alignment, interpretability, evaluations, governance) and its open problems; strong operational instincts; an entrepreneurial, initiative-taking approach to judgement calls about people, partnerships and priorities; and clear written communication. NICE TO HAVE: prior experience at an AI lab, AI safety organisation, university group, training programme or grantmaker; a background in education, talent development or community building; enough ML or alignment literacy to follow a paper's argument; policy literacy on the AI governance landscape; or a background in finance, law or another professional field Collider wants to build pipelines into. PROCESS: apply via the form in the job document by 23 August 2026 (applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and an offer may be made before the deadline, so applying early is advised), then a 15 to 25 minute screening call with hiring partner Impact Ops, an interview with the prospective manager, a paid one-day in-person work trial at the Collider coworking space, and 2 to 3 references. Reports to the Director.

grants.title: CPR Center for Performance Research: Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
grants.location: Brooklyn, New York City, USA. RESTRICTED: NYC-based artists only; CPR does not sponsor visas, and residents must remain NYC-based for the whole cycle.
grants.amount: $2,000 stipend, 20 free hours of rehearsal space, up to 150 subsidised rehearsal hours across CPR's two studios with priority and advance booking, presentation slots in the OPEN LAB and OPEN AiR programmes, and access to technical equipment and production support. No application fee.
grants.duration: One year, January to December 2027
grants.description: CPR's year-long Artist-in-Residence programme supports six New York City-based artists working across contemporary dance, performance and time-based art. The organisation values experimental approaches to content, form and aesthetics and explicitly encourages risk-taking, interdisciplinarity and the unexpected, so process-led and hard-to-categorise work is in scope rather than a liability. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $2,000 stipend; 20 free hours of rehearsal space plus up to 150 further subsidised hours in CPR's two studios, with priority and advance calendar access; participation in OPEN LAB (facilitated embodied workshops and feedback showings) and OPEN AiR (solo or shared presentations of current work); and access to technical equipment and production support. ELIGIBILITY: artists must be based in New York City and remain so throughout the cycle (no visa sponsorship); must have had work publicly presented before; must not have held a CPR residency in the last five years; and current undergraduates are not eligible. Individuals, companies, collaboratives and collectives may all apply, each counting as a single residency. CPR strongly encourages applications from BIPOC, LGBTQ+, immigrant and disabled artists and from artists across generations. APPLICATION: a Google Form with narrative answers on the artist's central research focus and its alignment with CPR's values; drafting answers in a separate document first is recommended. Selection is by an independent panel of artists, curators and arts leaders. Deadline: Monday 24 August 2026 at 5pm ET; late submissions are not accepted. Notifications November 2026. Questions: applications@cprnyc.org.

grants.title: Trusted Creator Fellowship 2026 (News Creator Corps)
grants.organization: News Creator Corps (a project of the Good Information Foundation)
grants.location: Virtual, meeting once a week. RESTRICTED: US-based creators only.
grants.amount: $5,000 stipend on completing the programme. No application fee.
grants.duration: Roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026, virtual sessions once a week
grants.description: A short-term virtual fellowship from News Creator Corps that trains independent content creators in the tactical craft of journalism: fact-checking, sourcing and interviewing, applied directly to their own channels during the programme so the community they already serve gets more credible information. WHO IT IS FOR: independent creators with an engaged following on digital platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Substack, YouTube and similar) whose content is information-based and serves a specific community. It is explicitly not aimed at traditional journalists already trained in reporting fundamentals. STUDENT SEATS: three places in the autumn cohort are reserved for full-time college students aged 25 or younger, who get the same fellowship experience as everyone else. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $5,000 stipend on completion, weekly virtual sessions, and access to discussion forums with the cohort, trainers, staff and alumni. ELIGIBILITY: US-based only. KEY DATES: applications close 17 August 2026 at 11:59pm ET; notifications by the end of September 2026; programme runs roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026. Contact: creatorprogram@newscreatorcorps.org. Sibling programme to the Rural Creator Fellowship.

grants.title: Surface Design Association: Artist in Residence 2026-27 (virtual)
grants.location: Fully virtual. Open to US-based and international applicants; current SDA membership is required.
grants.amount: $2,000 studio stipend, plus up to $2,000 further compensation for programming work (SDA aims for roughly $4,000 in total per resident). No application fee, but applicants must be current SDA members (membership from $85 per year, $60 for students).
grants.duration: One year, virtual, October 2026 to August 2027
grants.description: The Surface Design Association's Artist in Residence programme is built to develop skills, open up relationships and support fiber and textile artists through a studio project that pushes their practice. The residency is entirely virtual and runs across a full year, which is the point: it removes the travel, housing and time-away barriers that keep many practitioners out of in-person residencies. One artist is selected annually by a panel of SDA staff, board members and committee volunteers. WHAT IT INVOLVES: studio visits across the year, social media programming, and meetings with the SDA community, plus further programming shaped around the resident's own skills and interests, which can include teaching online workshops, contributing to SDA publications, jurying exhibitions or joining panels. FUNDING: a $2,000 studio stipend for the project, plus up to $2,000 in additional compensation for programming work, targeting about $4,000 total. ELIGIBILITY: emerging, mid-career and established artists; US-based and international applicants welcome; students and professionals may apply; applicants must hold current SDA membership (from $85 per year, $60 for students). APPLICATION: a portfolio of 10 images with full artwork information (title, year, materials, technique, dimensions, photo credit), a detailed CV, essay responses on artistic goals, programming interests and professional development, and demographic information. No application fee. The 2026-27 cycle closes 14 August 2026.

grants.title: Waging Nonviolence Journalism Fellowship (Fall 2026)
grants.location: Remote, with a flexible self-directed schedule. RESTRICTED: US-based writers.
grants.amount: $500 initial stipend plus $250 per published story, up to $1,750 in total. No application fee.
grants.duration: Five months (Fall 2026), remote and self-directed; five monthly feature articles of at least 1,500 words each
grants.description: The first Waging Nonviolence Fellowship is a five-month remote journalism programme for writers reporting on social movements, peace, justice and nonviolent action. It is framed as journalistic training: fellows work closely with senior editor Jessica Stites and editor-in-chief Eric Stoner and come out with a body of clips on an undercovered movement beat. WORK: five monthly feature articles of at least 1,500 words each for Waging Nonviolence, plus an initial meeting and check-ins as needed; fellows are expected to find their own stories, hit deadlines and respond promptly by email. PAY: a $500 stipend up front plus $250 per published story, so $1,750 across the full run. ELIGIBILITY: US-based; experience reporting on or analysing social movements; excellent writing and clean copy; genuine investment in peace and justice organising. Established connections to activist groups and communities, and knowledge of civil resistance history, theory, strategy and tactics, are preferred. APPLICATION: via a Google Form linked from the announcement; no resume or CV required. Deadline 10 August 2026. Contact: contact@wagingnonviolence.org.

grants.title: BigCi Environmental Awards 2026
grants.organization: Bilpin International Ground for Creative Initiatives (BigCi)
grants.location: Bilpin, New South Wales, Australia, on the edge of Wollemi National Park in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains, about 1.5 hours from Sydney. Open to Australian and international artists.
grants.amount: Two awards, each of AUD 5,000 prize money plus four weeks of free residency at BigCi, guided walks in the surrounding national parks and research assistance for the project. AUD 40 entry fee, non-refundable and payable with the submission.
grants.duration: Four-week residency at BigCi per winner
grants.description: BigCi's Environmental Awards are an annual prize for work that engages with the environment, open to Australian and international artists working in visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, literature, music, photography, filmmaking and curating. TWO WINNERS each receive four weeks of free residency at BigCi plus AUD 5,000 in prize money. BigCi sits on the edge of Wollemi National Park in the Greater Blue Mountains, an hour and a half from Sydney but geologically another world; winners explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Wollemi, Blue Mountains and Gardens of Stone National Parks on guided walks and are given research assistance relevant to their projects. At the end of their residencies they present the work at the BigCi Open Day. JUDGING: three independent judges, Lea Kannar-Lichtenberger (Australia), Brian Wallace (China) and Dan Gottlieb (USA). APPLICATION: an online submission form (Wufoo) linked from the awards page, with a non-refundable AUD 40 entry fee paid at the time of submission. KEY DATES: submissions close 2 August 2026; winners announced 22 August 2026. Enquiries via the contact form at bigci.org/contact.

grants.title: American Academy in Berlin: Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027-28
grants.location: Berlin, Germany, at the Hans Arnhold Center. RESTRICTED: fellowships are open only to citizens and permanent residents of the United States.
grants.amount: Monthly stipend of USD 5,000, plus roundtrip airfare, accommodation at or near the Hans Arnhold Center, partial board, in-house library services and professional networking opportunities. Roughly two dozen fellowships awarded each year. No application fee.
grants.duration: One full academic semester (about 4 months). Fall runs mid-August to mid-December; spring runs late January to late May.
grants.description: The American Academy in Berlin is an independent, nonprofit institute for advanced study in the arts, humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and public policy, whose primary mission is to strengthen the cultural and intellectual ties between the United States and Germany. Each year, after a rigorous selection process, the Academy awards roughly two dozen semester-long Berlin Prize fellowships to individuals who demonstrate excellence in their fields. DISCIPLINES: applications are welcome across the humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and various areas of public policy. The Academy generally encourages projects addressing pressing issues of the day, specifically naming democracy, security, technology and society (especially AI), energy including climate, and global order. Dedicated fellowships also support projects in Jewish studies, German studies, and public health and biotechnology. Project proposals need not focus on Germany, but candidates should explain how a residency in Berlin would enhance their work. NOT ACCEPTED: proposals in mathematics or the natural sciences. NOTE FOR ARTISTS: visual artists and composers are invited through separate, nomination-based competitions, so there is no open application route for them here. ELIGIBILITY: fellowships are restricted to citizens and permanent residents of the United States. Both emerging and established figures are eligible. PhD holders qualify as emerging scholars with a strong record of peer-reviewed work beyond the dissertation; candidates in non-academic fields such as journalism, filmmaking and policy need a significant record of publication or production; fiction and nonfiction writers must have published at least one book with a reputable press. WHAT FELLOWS DO: fellows present their work to audiences in and around Berlin through lectures, readings, public discussions, performances and film screenings, and should be willing to engage with relevant German institutions, organizations and the media; these activities are integral to the Academy's mission of fostering transatlantic dialogue. APPLICATION MATERIALS: a project proposal of 1,500 to 1,750 words plus a one-page bibliography; a curriculum vitae of up to 10 pages; two writing samples totalling no more than 60 pages; and three letters of recommendation, which are due 2 October 2026. DEADLINE: Friday 25 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Eastern Time (18:00 Central European Time). TIMELINE: all candidates are notified of the competition outcome by email in late March 2027; the 2027-28 Berlin Prize recipients are announced in May 2027.

grants.title: AIXI Labs: Research Fellowship (rolling, quarterly rounds)
grants.location: Fully remote, open worldwide; fellows may also work from the organisation's London base in the United Kingdom.
grants.amount: GBP 2,000 to GBP 3,500 per month stipend, plus a compute budget for machine-learning work. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Roughly one quarter (about 3 months) per fellowship. Quarterly rounds, rolling applications. Renewal possible in exceptional cases.
grants.description: AIXI Labs is a small London-based non-profit doing AI safety research grounded in algorithmic information theory. Its stated position is that most AI research today is either mathematically clean but narrow, or practical but too opaque for rigorous safety analysis; the lab targets a third category, methods general enough to describe powerful agents and provable enough to support real safety claims, using AIXI (the theoretical model of unbounded artificial superintelligence) and then porting the strongest of those ideas to modern LLM-based agents. The fellowship is a quarterly, rolling programme for researchers who want to work on this agenda under close mentorship from the core team: Cole Wyeth (Founder and Executive Director), Marcus Hutter (Research Director) and Aram Ebtekar (Founding Research Scientist). Fellows pursue a focused research project over roughly a quarter and receive a monthly stipend plus a compute budget for machine-learning work. The fellowship is fully remote, so fellows may work from anywhere in the world or from the London base. RESPONSIBILITIES: pursue a self-directed research project aligned with the lab's algorithmic-information-theoretic approach to AI safety, spanning anything from foundational theory to empirical tests with LLM-based agents; shape the project direction around your own strengths and interests, as the lab supports a range of work within this framework; and contribute papers, blog posts or other written output communicating results to the broader AI safety and ML research communities. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: a research background at the level of a current PhD student (for primarily empirical projects, a master's-level command of the relevant mathematics paired with substantial industry or applied research experience can also qualify); solid grounding in probability, statistics, information theory and reinforcement learning, sufficient to engage seriously with AIXI-style theoretical models (prior expertise in algorithmic information theory or AIXI is NOT required); strong verbal and written communication skills; genuine motivation to reduce existential risk from advanced AI and enthusiasm for the lab's kind of work. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: publications at top ML, AI or theory venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ALT or COLT, though the lab values the strength of your best work over volume; background in algorithmic information theory, computability theory, learning theory or related theoretical computer science; experience fine-tuning, evaluating or red-teaming LLM-based and/or RL agents; prior engagement with the UAI/AIXI community or related fields, including members of the lab's online reading groups. APPLICATIONS are reviewed on a rolling basis and previous applicants remain eligible for later rounds.

grants.title: Privacy Camp 2026 (EDRi): Call for Sessions, The Origins of Future Technologies
grants.organization: European Digital Rights (EDRi), with LSTS at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center
grants.location: Brussels, Belgium, and online (hybrid). Event on 13 October 2026.
grants.amount: NO speaker fee or honorarium. Where needed, up to EUR 400 per speaker or session organiser towards transport to and accommodation in Brussels, reimbursed against invoices and travel tickets; those with organisational support are encouraged to cover their own expenses. No budget beyond this cap. Free to propose and free to attend (registration open).
grants.duration: One-day conference on 13 October 2026. Average session length 50 minutes.
grants.description: Privacy Camp holds its 14th edition on 13 October 2026 in Brussels and online, organised by European Digital Rights (EDRi) with the Research Group on Law, Science, Technology & Society (LSTS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center. THEME: 'The Origins of Future Technologies: Towards communities of digital self-determination'. The call starts from the premise that digital futures do not appear from nowhere but are built through land, labour, capital, infrastructure, law, public money, political choices and social struggle, and asks where technologies come from, who gets to shape them, and what conditions make digital self-determination possible. It situates this against the EU's 2026 Tech Sovereignty Package (semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and data centres) and the wider deregulatory agenda including the Digital Omnibus, the AI Omnibus and reforms affecting data protection, privacy, labour and environmental safeguards, asking whose version of sovereignty is actually being discussed. TOPIC AREAS: (1) Material conditions in the production of technologies, covering the natural resources needed across the supply chain (critical components such as semiconductors, water for data centres) and how GDPR, ePrivacy and AI Act safeguards shape the material conditions of AI from data extraction and biometric processing through to data centres, labour and public infrastructure; labour conditions, including who mines critical materials, union-busting across the tech supply chain, and coalitions between tech workers, unions, migrant justice groups, climate movements and digital rights organisations; and capital, meaning the venture capital forces driving the current AI hype and consolidating through defence, security and militarisation. (2) Political vision in the use of technologies, covering military use and how militarisation and securitisation shape the EU deregulation debate, and the political ideologies driving technology development, including what digital self-determination means for communities facing racialised discrimination, surveillance, occupation, border violence, workplace control or environmental harm. (3) Moving technologies forward through communities, covering community innovation for digital self-determination (distributed and self-hosted data storage, AI built by and for community needs, community-led, public or cooperative digital infrastructure); law, deregulation and rights (resisting the Digital Omnibus and specifically the Data Omnibus, defending GDPR and ePrivacy safeguards, protecting access, transparency and automated decision-making rights, enforcing existing digital laws, supporting collective litigation, and challenging the framing of rights as obstacles to EU competitiveness); and building power by connecting grassroots movements across tech worker organising, labour, migrant, LGBTQIA+, climate, economic justice and landback movements. FORMATS: interactive workshops are particularly encouraged, meaning small-group work, peer exchange and collaboration across sectors, coalitions and disciplines, moving from talk to strategic action; panel discussions are also welcome, especially those centring diverse voices and grounded lived experience with room for meaningful audience engagement. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: state a clear objective for the session and what a good outcome would be; make it as interactive as possible; support a diversity of voices and multiple perspectives; average session length is 50 minutes; propose the format that actually suits the idea rather than forcing a panel into a workshop or vice versa. For workshops, make the objectives, structure and facilitation clear and have participants work together in small groups towards a specific goal; the organisers provide additional guidance, support and feedback for workshops. For panels, list a maximum of 4 speakers covering academia, civil society and decision-maker perspectives, and indicate which speakers have confirmed at least in principle. TIMELINE: proposals due via the online form by 10 August 2026 at 09:00 CEST; the Content Committee notifies applicants before 21 August 2026; confirmation to proceed required by 25 August; draft programme published 4 September; speakers and final session description confirmed by 10 September at the latest (earlier confirmation improves the odds that the EUR 400 reimbursement budget covers speaker travel and accommodation); final programme published 28 September. The 2026 Content Committee is Andreea Belu (EDRi), Gloria González Fuster (LSTS, VUB), Jill Toh (Racism and Technology Center), Sanne Stevens (Justice, Equity and Technology Project) and Alexandra Giannopoulou (DFF). Programme enquiries: andreea.belu@edri.org. Venue and reimbursement enquiries: guillermo.peris@edri.org.

grants.title: ESWA Digital Rights Gathering 2026: The (W)horrors Edition (Barcelona)
grants.location: Barcelona, Spain. Gathering runs 2-5 November 2026 (travel day out 1 November, travel day home 5 November).
grants.amount: PARTICIPANTS: fully funded, with travel, accommodation and food covered for all selected participants. SESSION FACILITATORS: EUR 300 per 90-minute session, plus travel, accommodation and meals covered. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Three days of sessions, 2-4 November 2026, within a 1-5 November travel window
grants.description: NO PUBLISHED CLOSING DATE: the call gives no application deadline, so the operative cutoff is the gathering itself on 2-5 November 2026; apply early. The European Sex Workers' Rights Alliance (ESWA) brings back its Digital Rights Gathering in 2026 as The (W)horrors Edition, in Barcelona just after Halloween. It is a capacity and community-building space by and for sex workers, convened to confront the surveillance, censorship and digital violence they face online and to imagine and build more resilient digital futures. A limited number of spaces is reserved for allies working in adjacent digital rights and harm reduction spaces to host sessions. TWO CALLS ARE OPEN. (1) CALL FOR PARTICIPANTS, for sex workers who want to deepen their knowledge of digital rights, online safety and community resilience. Requirements: be a current or former sex worker who is also a member of an organisation in ESWA's network; be available for three days of interactive sessions, skill-sharing and collective learning on 2, 3 and 4 November, and free from 1 November (travel out) through 5 November (travel home), even though some final-day sessions are optional. Selected participants receive full funding covering travel, accommodation and food. (2) CALL FOR TRAINERS AND SESSION PROPOSALS, for facilitators, trainers and educators experienced in digital rights, online safety or sex worker-led organising, who want to deliver an interactive workshop, skill-share or creative session. Sessions run 90 minutes and are compensated at EUR 300 per session, with travel, accommodation and meals covered. Open to current or former sex workers, and to allies with experience in digital rights, digital discrimination, digital security and related fields. SESSION STRANDS: Digital (W)horrors, naming the threats faced online and unpacking how surveillance, censorship and platform policy work against sex workers, including shadowbanning and algorithmic censorship, over-zealous content moderation, law enforcement and third-party surveillance, deplatforming, non-consensual data scraping and retention, and the platforms and policies that enable them; Building Resilience, practical hands-on skills covering open source and privacy-respecting software, how and why to divest from Big Tech platforms, alternative and encrypted communication tools, digital security basics such as protecting data, devices and identity, and other harm-reduction strategies for working and organising online; Imagining Better Futures, creative forward-looking sessions on what a sex worker friendly internet would look like, including prototyping inclusive digital tools, platforms and spaces built by and for sex workers, new apps, alternative social platforms, community-owned tech, and speculative design exercises; Resourcing the Group, sessions focused on care and resilience, including writing and reflection, grounding and somatic exercises, tools for self-care and sustainability in activism, and space for radical rest. The organisers welcome grounded, political and creative contributions from anyone who would like to lead a session. Separate application forms for participants and for session proposals are linked from the call page. Questions: ana@eswalliance.org.

grants.title: Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe: Strengthening Movements for Gender Equality (2026 call)
grants.organization: Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe (hosted by the Network of European Foundations)
grants.location: European Union, United Kingdom, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. All coalition partners must be based and operating in these countries.
grants.amount: EUR 2,700,000 total across the call. Between EUR 225,000 and EUR 450,000 per grant over 3 years (EUR 75,000 to EUR 150,000 per year). Project support including salary and overhead costs; overheads capped at 20 percent. 6 to 12 coalitions expected to be funded. Free to apply.
grants.duration: 3 years, January 2027 to December 2029. Renewal possible at the end of the cycle subject to budget.
grants.description: NOTE: this is a gender-equality movement-building fund rather than an arts or technology programme, and it is coalition-only (no individual applicants). Relevance to creative or tech practice runs through the narrative-change and digital-storytelling strand of the call. The Alliance for Gender Equality in Europe, a philanthropic initiative created in 2021 and hosted by the Network of European Foundations, is launching an open call under its forthcoming Strengthening Movements Fund. The Alliance is composed of the Bodossaki Foundation, Fondation BNP Paribas, Fondation CHANEL, Fondazione con il Sud, Fondation de France, Fondation RAJA-Danièle Marcovici, King Baudouin Foundation and L'Oréal Fund for Women; this particular fund is backed by all of those except Fondation BNP Paribas. OBJECTIVE: to foster collaboration and solidarity within European intersectional and grassroots movements so that they can collectively advance gender equality in Europe in the long term. The call follows a 2025 Alliance-commissioned mapping of European gender-equality movements (30 in-depth interviews plus contextual research) which found movements under-resourced because philanthropic funding frameworks are misaligned with their needs; the fund is designed to replace short-term reactive funding with proactive long-term support. OUTCOMES SOUGHT: community organising reinforced at local or national level; pan-European feminist collaborations and solidarity strengthened; alliances between gender equality and other social justice movements expanded; pro-gender-equality narratives and voices amplified in local, national, regional or digital spaces; policy debates informed by feminist and gender equality movements. ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE (non-exhaustive): national, regional or pan-European convenings and collaborative projects where groups co-create joint strategies; joint campaigns between feminist movements and allied movements (climate justice, anti-racism, LGBTQI+, disability rights); narrative-change training for grassroots groups covering framing, messaging, digital tools and digital storytelling; cross-border coalitions advocating EU institutions or national governments; facilitated virtual or in-person convenings to work through internal tensions and build trust; translating academic research on anti-gender efforts into movement strategies. ELIGIBILITY: collective proposals with at least 3 organisations per coalition (no maximum); legally registered non-profits (NGOs, civil society organisations, social enterprises, national or regional funds); based and operating in the target countries; small and medium grassroots organisations, defined by annual budget under EUR 450,000 (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, UK) or under EUR 300,000 (Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Serbia). Intermediary organisations and networks are exempt from the budget thresholds but must apply in coalition with grassroots organisations, with the budget fairly distributed among all partners. Coalitions must be community-led (majority of leadership roles held by members of the community supported, and/or participatory approaches), work with marginalised women, transgender, non-binary and gender non-conforming people, use gender transformative approaches, and hold an intersectional perspective. Proposals must be completed in English. Each organisation may submit only one application, as lead or as partner. One organisation per coalition acts as lead, is the primary contact and is legally responsible for the grant; leads are invited to networking, peer-learning and capacity-strengthening activities. SCORING (100 points): relevance to the call objective 20; demonstrated track record in strengthening movements 20 (learnings valued as well as achievements); strong impact 25 (must contribute to at least one of the five outcomes, with clear measurement); ability to work collaboratively and inclusively with partners 20 (including fair budget repartition); quality and feasibility 15. PROCESS: two stages. Stage 1 opened 29 June 2026 and closes 7 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST, submitted in English via the online platform (a PDF of the form is downloadable for reference only). Pre-selection results by email 14 September 2026; stage 2 runs 16 September to 23 October 2026 and includes due-diligence contact from Alliance staff; final results by email in December 2026; grants start January 2027. The Alliance is piloting a participatory selection process for this call, with grant-making decisions made jointly by a committee of funders and non-funders holding equal decision-making power. Q&A webinars: 6 July 2026 at 14:00 CEST and 15 July 2026 at 10:00 CEST (registration in advance; both have passed). An updated FAQ is published on the call page.

grants.title: Resynthesising the Traditional: Fragmented Distance (CTM x NOPA Artistic Lab, Armenia)
grants.location: Yerevan / Armenia. Preference to artists who reside in or have a diasporic connection to Armenia, Georgia, Iran, Iraq, Syria, the Anatolian region, the Caspian Sea, the Levant, and the Northern Caucasus.
grants.amount: Participants supported with a travel budget of up to EUR 450 each, accommodation and catering for the duration of the lab, a NOPA Festival pass, and a per diem. Visa fees supported when required, and letters of invitation provided. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Eight-day lab, 1 to 10 October 2026 (arrival 1 October, departure 10 October)
grants.description: Fragmented Distance is the latest artistic lab from CTM Festival's Resynthesising the Traditional initiative (co-curated by Stas Sharifulla and CTM), taking place 1 to 10 October 2026 in Armenia in collaboration with NOPA, a festival dedicated to sonic arts and experimental music. Resynthesising the Traditional explores how musicians, sound artists, and researchers can critically engage with traditions and heritage, using resynthesis (a computer-music method that analyses sounds to extract their fundamental components) as a guiding metaphor, and resisting conservative views of culture as frozen or untouchable; the lab is an open toolbox helping artists connect to 'the traditional' outside of exoticisation, cultural essentialism, and uneven power dynamics. This edition focuses on diaspora, memory, displacement, transmission, and hybridity, responding to Armenia's shift into a point of arrival for refugees and diasporic communities and to the displacement following the ethnic cleansing of Artsakh / Nagorno-Karabakh. It invites artists whose work resynthesising traditional practices addresses how traditional musical forms are maintained, altered, or recontextualised as they move across geographies and generations, how in-betweenness and non-belonging can be articulated through sound, and how sonic expression can act as rehumanisation. THE LAB (eight days, 10:00-19:00 daily) includes theory and practice workshops, individual closed oral presentations, solo public performances (15-20 minutes), specialist inputs, guided sonic improvisations, field trips, and feedback sessions. Following the lab, participants may propose new solo or collaborative work to the Resynthesising the Traditional team; selected works are shortlisted for commission and presentation at CTM Festival Berlin and/or NOPA Festival Yerevan. CONDITIONS: solo artists/projects only; applicants should have an existing practice tied to (re)connecting with traditional ideas and sounds through a contemporary lens, and clear next steps; working knowledge of English recommended. SELECTION: a pre-selection committee (Varoujan Chetirian, Stas Sharifulla, Taica Replansky) creates a shortlist, from which up to six participants are chosen by lab co-hosts Cinna Peyghamy, Vardan Baghdasaryan, and Varoujan Chetirian. TIMELINE: deadline 8 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST; results by early September 2026; lab 1 to 10 October 2026. Apply with a portfolio (PDF, max 10 pages) and an audio link; questions to team@nopa.art. Free to apply.

grants.title: CTM 2027 Research Networking Day: Open Call for Presentations (Berlin)
grants.location: Berlin, Germany. On-site presentations within the CTM festival's Discourse programme, in English.
grants.amount: No funding for travel or accommodation. Participants receive a CTM 2027 festival pass, a catered lunch on the day of presentations, and a group dinner. Entrance to the event is free; free to apply.
grants.duration: One-day event, Sunday 24 January 2027 (within CTM 2027, 22-31 January 2027)
grants.description: The Research Networking Day (RND) is an exchange platform for graduate or postgraduate students and independent artists conducting self-guided research traversing audio, arts, media, design, and related theoretical disciplines. The RND 2027 open call seeks innovative and critical submissions from all areas of study addressing the CTM 2027 festival theme 'Process...ing'. Nine selected candidates give short ten-minute presentations within different modules, linked by discussion rounds at the end of each module, offering an international platform to exchange with colleagues and researchers working on related ideas; research is also shared via audio/video after the festival on CTM's YouTube and SoundCloud channels. This edition takes place in collaboration with the Design Academy Eindhoven, Universitat der Kunste Berlin (UdK), and Leuphana University Luneburg. CONDITIONS: presentations take place on-site within the festival's Discourse programme, in English; applications are for individual (solo) presentations only (no duos or groups). As in previous years, no funding is available for travel and accommodation; participants receive a CTM 2027 festival pass, a catered lunch on the day, and a group dinner. Entrance to the event is free. KEY DATES: application deadline 25 October 2026 at 23:59 CET; programme announced mid to late November 2026; RND 2027 event Sunday 24 January 2027; CTM 2027 runs 22 to 31 January 2027.

grants.title: Design Trust Seed, Feature & Impact Grants (Hong Kong / Greater Bay Area)
grants.location: Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area. Open to applicants based in the region or seeking support for design projects related to it, including international applicants.
grants.amount: Seed Grant: HKD 50,000. Feature Grant: capped at HKD 300,000, awarded annually upon special consideration. Impact Grant: case-by-case, for former grantees. Full or partial funding on a case-by-case basis. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Two grant cycles annually (deadlines 20 April and 20 October); apply 3 to 6 months before project commencement
grants.description: Design Trust offers grants to individual designers, curators, collectives, and non-profit organisations for projects and activities relevant to various design disciplines, supporting work relevant to the context and content of Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area (the Special Administrative Regions of Hong Kong and Macao and the nine Guangdong municipalities of Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Foshan, Huizhou, Dongguan, Zhongshan, Jiangmen, and Zhaoqing). It supports innovative, thought-provoking investigations across design disciplines from graphics, media, and wearables to architecture and the built environment, including exhibitions, research projects, and creative installations that advocate the positive role of design in the region. THREE GRANTS: (1) SEED GRANT (HKD 50,000) fosters experimentation, testing, and sharing, awarded to individuals kick-starting a meaningful project with social, educational, economical, or environmental impact; supports emerging designers, young scholars, and projects in the pipeline needing additional resources, including research and prototypes focused on Hong Kong and Greater Bay Area issues to be showcased at international venues, symposia, or biennales. (2) FEATURE GRANT (capped at HKD 300,000, awarded annually upon special consideration) fosters cross-disciplinary projects on the Greater Bay Area with wide-reaching audiences, often sited at an exhibition or biennale of international standing, supporting exchange between a Hong Kong/China-based collective and an internationally renowned cultural institution. (3) IMPACT GRANT supports public-facing, community-based projects led by former Design Trust grant recipients, fellows, and mentees with a proven track record; considered case-by-case (contact grantapplication@designtrust.hk). ELIGIBILITY: individuals, collectives, and certified non-profit organisations either based in the Greater Bay Area or seeking support for design projects related to the region. Individuals or collectives who have completed two Feature Grants or three Seed Grants should apply for the Impact Grant instead. APPLICATION: two cycles annually, deadlines 20 April and 20 October (late submissions roll to the next cycle); apply at least 3 to 6 months before the project's commencement. Design Trust may provide full or partial funding on a case-by-case basis.

grants.title: Developh Tropical Internet Research Fellowship (Philippines / Southeast Asia)
grants.location: Remote / Philippines and broader Southeast Asia. Applicants welcome from any location; preference to those within the Philippines, particularly outside Metro Manila.
grants.amount: PHP 20,000 (~USD 300) stipend, with a potential additional stipend depending on fieldwork/research needs. Plus editorial and publishing support (coding, design, hosting for the final output), online cohort sessions, check-ins with the Developh team and guest critics, and free access to Developh events and workshops for the fellowship period. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Research and writing September 2026 to January 2027 (5 months); publication and presentations March to April 2027 onwards
grants.description: Developh invites applications for its inaugural Tropical Internet Research Fellowship, supporting researchers, writers, and artist-technologists at any career stage who are investigating the cultural and material conditions of the internet across the Philippines and Southeast Asia and are interested in producing written work. The fellowship runs seasonally (every 1-2 years) to support new writing about the 'tropical internet': the online as experienced from the tropical regions of the Philippines and broader Southeast Asia, concerned with heat, extremes, monsoons, distance, islandedness, improvisation, pluralities, and diasporas. It nurtures work examining how the internet is lived, built, resisted, and felt across the region, welcoming research on infrastructures, digital labor, rural-urban internet inequities, algorithmic cultures, online intimacies, and the entangled relationships between land, technology, and the body, and how colonial, corporate, and extractive forces shape infrastructures for connection. WHO SHOULD APPLY: researchers, writers, designers, artists, and technologists with strong ties to the Philippines or broader Southeast Asia; applicants welcome from any present location, with preference to those within the Philippines, particularly outside Metro Manila. Work may relate to an academic thesis, but the produced artifact must be a distinct new work separate from the thesis. COMMITMENTS: produce an output by January 2027 (suggested minimum ~2000 words, in English, Filipino, or any Philippine language); publish with Developh by March-April 2027 with editorial and publication support; present findings by March-April 2027; share citations and research notes for a collective reference library; attend three cohort group meetings; and participate in editorial review and feedback cycles (prototypes and interim essays are encouraged; a fully finished output is not required). FELLOWS RECEIVE: a PHP 20,000 (~USD 300) stipend, with a potential additional stipend depending on fieldwork/research needs; peer learning through online cohort sessions; check-ins with the Developh team and guest critics; editorial and publishing support (coding, design, hosting); and free access to Developh events and workshops for the fellowship period. TIMELINE: application deadline 22 August 2026; writing and research September 2026 to January 2027; publication and presentations March 2027 onwards. Apply via the Google Form. Free to apply.

grants.title: LATITUDE Artist in Residence 2027 (Chicago)
grants.location: Chicago, Illinois, USA. No housing stipend offered.
grants.amount: One-month production residency for 8-10 artists: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation, staff training and guidance on tech, an organised public event, and lifetime free lab access. No housing stipend. Free to apply before 16 August 2026; a $20 donation thereafter.
grants.duration: One month (residency takes place in 2027)
grants.description: The LATITUDE Artist in Residence program (started in 2013) is a one-month production residency where 8-10 artists are granted full access to LATITUDE's facilities and community to develop their practice. Its focus is supporting artists who want to use LATITUDE's printing and scanning services to expand their practice, regardless of medium or experience; past residents include photographers, painters, performance artists, new media artists, and sculptors. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation and 24/7 access, training and guidance on tech from staff, an organised public event to present new work, and lifetime free lab access. LATITUDE does not offer a housing stipend but will help schedule studio visits during the month. PUBLIC PROGRAMMING: during the residency each artist puts on one community programming event (past examples include panel discussions, artist talks, performances, workshops, and critiques; a gallery space is available for curation) and is asked to act as a mentor to the community, sharing insights and creative methods. WHO SHOULD APPLY: artists interested in production, education, and tech experimentation; no prior printing experience, art education, or media specificity is required, though professionalism and communication are expected. 2027 PANEL COMMITTEE: Yechen Zhao, B. Ingrid Olson, Teri Carson. TIMELINE: applications open 1 August 2026 (free before 16 August, a $20 donation thereafter) and close 1 September 2026 at 12pm (noon) CST; the selection committee reviews in September, meets to decide finalists in October, and acceptances are sent early November 2026. Apply at latitudechicago.org/artist-in-residence.

grants.title: G.MAP Digital Art Culture Lab 2026: Project Lab (Gwangju, South Korea)
grants.location: Jeonnam-Gwangju, South Korea. International applicants welcome (Track 2 only).
grants.amount: Track 2 (Interdisciplinary Creation): creation and production grant up to KRW 30,000,000 per team, plus accommodation, equipment, studio space, production and travel support, exhibition on G.MAP spaces and large-scale public media platforms (LED Wall, city media facades), and publication. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Five-month creation support program, August to December 2026
grants.description: The Gwangju Media Art Platform (G.MAP), an institution of Gwangju, UNESCO Creative City of Media Arts, invites artists and teams working in digital art to the 2026 Digital Art Culture Lab: Project Lab, a five-month creation support program (August to December 2026) covering the entire creative process from idea development through production, showcase and archiving. WHO CAN APPLY: artists and groups in digital art wishing to create interdisciplinary projects using digital technology (all members aged 19+; international applicants welcome). Focus areas: digital art, media art, generative art, AI, interactive art, XR, AR, VR, interdisciplinary, art and technology. SELECTION: 14 teams total across two tracks: Track 1 Digital Transformation (7 artists/teams) and Track 2 Interdisciplinary Creation (7 teams). INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS CAN APPLY FOR TRACK 2 ONLY. SUPPORT: creation and production grant up to KRW 30,000,000 per team for Track 2, two online mentoring sessions, and a showcase in G.MAP exhibition spaces and on large-scale public media platforms including the G.MAP LED Wall and city media facades. KEY DATES: application period 21 July to 9 August 2026, 6 PM KST; results announced 14 August 2026; program period 20 August to 31 December 2026. Overseas participants (Track 2) must attend two in-person meetings in Jeonnam-Gwangju. HOW TO APPLY: submit the application form and portfolio (PDF) by email to uartlabseoul@gmail.com. More info at urbanartlab.org/opencall. Free to apply.

grants.title: La Résidence du Festival de Cannes (Cinéma de Demain): Screenwriting Residency in Paris
grants.organization: Festival de Cannes (Cinéma de Demain / La Résidence)
grants.location: Paris, France. Candidates must not be residents or citizens of France.
grants.amount: Fully supported: a place of residence in central Paris, a personalised script-writing programme, and a collective programme of forums with film industry professionals. Directors present at the CNC pavilion in Cannes, where the CNC awards a EUR 5,000 grant to one director per session. Free to apply.
grants.duration: Four and a half months per session (two sessions a year)
grants.description: La Résidence of the Festival de Cannes (part of Cinéma de Demain, formerly La Cinéfondation) invites 12 directors each year to write their screenplay in Paris. The programme provides a place of residence in the heart of Paris, a personalised programme accompanying the writing of their scripts, and a collective programme of forums with film industry professionals. The 12 directors from the two annual sessions present their projects at the CNC pavilion in Cannes, giving 10-minute presentations to an audience of professionals and a jury of three film industry personalities; the CNC then awards a EUR 5,000 grant to one director from each session, based on the project that most inspires the jury. The Cinef & Résidence offices serve as a hub where directors meet and schedule private meetings with potential producers. ELIGIBILITY: open to young filmmakers who have made one or several short films and no more than one feature film; candidates must NOT be residents or citizens of France. Selected filmmakers must stay at the Résidence in Paris for the full session. SESSIONS: two per year, each lasting four and a half months, the first running 15 March to 31 July and the second 1 October to 15 February. Artistic fields: film, writing, interdisciplinary. Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 16:00 UTC. Free to apply.

grants.title: Fucina Futura 2027 Residency (Marostica, Italy)
grants.organization: Futura Association (Fucina Futura), supported by Culture Moves Europe
grants.location: Marostica, Italy (one hour from Venice). Open to artists resident in a Creative Europe country except Italy.
grants.amount: Fully funded: daily fee to cover living expenses, travel costs covered, and shared house accommodation provided (supported by Culture Moves Europe). No application fee.
grants.duration: One month, 12 April to 12 May 2027; three residents hosted together
grants.description: Fucina Futura is an artist residency in Marostica, a small town about an hour from Venice, offering a peaceful setting to develop research in close contact with nature and the local community. The project spans two locations: the home designed by internationally renowned illustrator Elena Xausa near the historic centre, and the atelier Fucina Ai Gorghi by beloved local painter Daniele Marcon, ideal for large-scale installations. Led by visual artist Lavinia and curator Sofia (Futura Association), the program invites residents to develop projects that engage with the community and the working location, and encourages artists of any discipline to make full use of the large atelier. The central goal is the 'restitution' to citizens, fostering cultural exchange and community inclusion: this final phase is tailored to each artist and can take the form of an exhibition, performance, workshop, screening, talk or informal sharing session, prioritising direct dialogue with the public and the contemporary renewal of local tradition. THREE residents are hosted together from 12 April to 12 May 2027 and share a spacious house; they receive a daily fee to cover living expenses, and travel expenses are also covered. Made possible by Culture Moves Europe. ELIGIBILITY: only artists residing in one of the Creative Europe countries EXCEPT ITALY may apply. Creative Europe covers the 27 EU member states (other than Italy), plus Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, and includes the EU's Overseas Countries and Territories and Outermost Regions (Greenland; French Guiana, French Polynesia, French Southern and Antarctic Territories, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, New Caledonia, Reunion, Saint Barthelemy, Saint-Martin, St. Pierre and Miquelon, Wallis and Futuna; Azores, Madeira; Canary Islands; Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Maarten, Sint Eustatius). TIMELINE: apply via the Google Form by 20 August 2026; selected artists informed by 30 August and must confirm participation by 8 September 2026.

grants.title: ProAC / Fomento CultSP: Edital 05/2026, Electronic Games Development and Publishing
grants.organization: Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Industria Criativas do Estado de Sao Paulo (ProAC)
grants.location: Sao Paulo state, Brazil. Open only to legal entities headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years.
grants.amount: BRL 300,000 (around USD 55,000 / EUR 50,000) per selected project, 20 projects total across two modules, from a BRL 6,000,000 pool. Registration is free.
grants.duration: Module I funds game development; Module II funds finalisation and publishing of an existing game.
grants.description: Sao Paulo state's ProAC scheme runs one of the largest dedicated public funds for game development in Latin America. Edital 05/2026 splits BRL 6,000,000 across two modules of ten projects each: Module I for developing electronic games, Module II for finalising and publishing them, at BRL 300,000 per project. At least six of the ten slots in each module are reserved for applicants based outside the state capital. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED AND NARROW: individuals cannot apply. Applicants must be legal entities, meaning private companies (for-profit or not-for-profit) or registered MEI microentrepreneurs, headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years, with artistic or cultural activity expressly stated in their founding documents. Applications close 27 July 2026 at 23:59:59 Brasilia time via fomento.sp.gov.br. Note this is a tight deadline.

grants.title: India Foundation for the Arts: Arts Research Programme (May 2026 Request for Proposals)
grants.location: India; project-based with no residency requirement. Open to Indian nationals only.
grants.amount: Up to INR 500,000 (around USD 5,700 / EUR 4,900) per project. Honorarium is capped at 35 percent of the budget. Institutional overhead, building costs, infrastructure and equipment purchases are excluded. No application fee.
grants.duration: Minimum 12 months, maximum 18 months.
grants.description: IFA's Arts Research Programme funds research into forms of knowing and thinking rooted in creative, scholarly or cultural practice. It explicitly welcomes experimental and self-reflexive methodologies, practice-based inquiry, interdisciplinary dialogue, community engagement, translation studies and work on marginalised narratives, with a shareable public outcome expected. Open to artists, scholars, curators, translators, educators and practitioner-researchers. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian nationals only, and PIO and OCI card holders are explicitly excluded; any collaborators must also be Indian nationals. Applicants need a PAN card and valid ID. PROCESS NOTE: this is a two-stage email application, not a web form. Applicants were expected to discuss the project concept with the Programme Officer (harshita@indiaifa.org) by 11 July 2026, with the final proposal, CV and budget breakdown emailed by 10 August 2026 at 23:59 IST, in an email no larger than 25 MB. Proposals may be written in any Indian language, including English.

grants.title: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation: Inlaks Fine Art Award 2027
grants.location: India. Open to Indian citizens currently living in India.
grants.amount: INR 300,000 (around USD 3,400 / EUR 2,950) for one year, plus a fully covered four-week art residency at an Indian art institution. No application fee.
grants.duration: Twelve months of independent practice, including a mandatory four-week residency within India.
grants.description: A one-year award enabling an emerging Indian visual artist to pursue independent practice, with a stipulation to attend a recognised art residency programme in India for four weeks during the year. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian citizens currently living in India, born on or after 1 January 1996, who are either recent graduates, postgraduates or final-year students of a leading Indian visual arts institute, or artists without those formal credentials but with a record of exhibition participation. First-year MA students are not eligible. Awardees submit progress reports at six months and on completion, plus documentation of the residency. Applications close 15 August 2026 at 23:59 IST via Submittable. Shortlisting is expected in late October 2026 with interviews in early November.

grants.title: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation: Inlaks Theatre Art Award 2027
grants.location: India. Open to Indian citizens.
grants.amount: INR 15,000 per month for up to 12 months, around INR 180,000 total (roughly USD 2,050 / EUR 1,780). No application fee.
grants.duration: Up to twelve months of skill enhancement, with six-month interim and final reporting.
grants.description: A skill-enhancement award for emerging Indian theatre practitioners, supporting participation in recognised training workshops, residencies and similar programmes rather than the production of a specific work. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian citizens born after 1 January 1991, with preference given to holders of a theatre degree from a leading Indian institution. Recipients report at the six-month mark and on completion. Applications close 15 August 2026 at 23:59 IST via Submittable. The foundation runs several other awards on adjacent deadlines, including the Inlaks-Attakkalari Dance Studentship (30 August 2026) and a two-month Inlaks Residency at the International Center of Photography in the USA for emerging Indian photographic practitioners (31 August 2026).

grants.title: Instituto Sacatar: Sacatar Fellowship 2027 (Bahia, Brazil)
grants.location: Itaparica island, Bahia, Brazil. Open to all nationalities.
grants.amount: Fully hosted residency: private bedroom with attached bathroom, three meals a day (except Saturday evenings, Sundays and Brazilian holidays), an individual studio suited to the discipline, weekly laundry, logistical support and airport transfer from Salvador. NO STIPEND, no airfare and no materials budget. USD 25 application fee. One French artist may additionally receive airfare and a stipend through Villa Fatumbi.
grants.duration: Approximately eight weeks; specific session dates are listed in the application.
grants.description: Brazil's longest-running artist residency, on the island of Itaparica across the bay from Salvador, hosting six to eight artists per session for roughly eight weeks. Open to all creative disciplines and, unusually for this region, to all nationalities, which makes it one of the few genuinely international residencies in Latin America. Sacatar provides full hosting (private room, three meals daily, individual studio, laundry, local logistics and connections) but explicitly does NOT provide a stipend, airfare to Salvador, art materials or discretionary local expenses, so applicants must fund their own travel. Individual artists only; group proposals are not accepted and former Sacatar Fellows may not reapply. COVID vaccination is required. NOTE: there is a USD 25 application fee. Apply through SlideRoom by 28 August 2026. Contact info@sacatar.org.

grants.title: Red Quincho: Beca Constelaciones 2026 (4th Edition)
grants.location: Rotating urban and rural Red Quincho spaces across Argentina; residency runs September to December 2026.
grants.amount: ARS 1,000,000 (around USD 690) per grant toward mobility, living costs and production, plus one month of lodging. 15 grants available. No application fee.
grants.duration: One-month residency split into two 15-day placements at different spaces.
grants.description: Beca Constelaciones is Red Quincho's mobility and production grant for artists, curators and researchers doing territory-based work, now in its fourth edition. Each recipient spends one month in residence, split into two 15-day placements at different member spaces across Argentina, pairing an urban and a rural context. The grant covers mobility, living costs and production, with lodging provided. Backed by Fundacion Williams, CCEBA and Fundacion Santander through the CABA Mecenazgo scheme. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: of the 15 grants, 13 are for people resident in Argentina and 2 are for people currently living in Spain. Artists, curators and researchers apply through separate forms; Spanish-based candidates face an additional jury evaluation. Deadline 9 August 2026 at 23:59 Argentina time.

grants.title: Marrakech IFF: Atlas Workshops 2026 (Films in Shooting or Post-Production)
grants.organization: Festival International du Film de Marrakech (Atlas Workshops)
grants.location: Online in October 2026, then onsite in Marrakech, Morocco, 22-26 November 2026, alongside the Marrakech International Film Festival.
grants.amount: No application fee. Participation in the online and onsite programme is covered. Cash prizes are awarded by a dedicated jury at the close of the Workshops; the festival does not publish the prize amounts on the call page.
grants.duration: Five-day online programme in October 2026, followed by a five-day onsite programme 22-26 November 2026.
grants.description: The Atlas Workshops are the Marrakech International Film Festival's industry and talent-development programme, running since 2018 and now in its 9th edition. This track is for feature films already in shooting or post-production. Selected teams get personalised mentoring tailored to each project across scriptwriting, production, distribution, editing and scoring, plus access to the festival's industry network, and compete for cash prizes decided by a dedicated jury. ELIGIBILITY: directors and producers who are from, or in the diaspora of, the Arab world or the African continent, working on their first, second or third feature (fiction, documentary or animation), with a production company attached. Open across that whole region, not restricted to Morocco. There is a separate Projects in Development track whose deadline (6 July 2026) has already passed for this edition. Deadline 31 August 2026.

grants.title: Marrakech IFF: Atlas Station 2026 (Producers Track)
grants.organization: Festival International du Film de Marrakech (Atlas Workshops)
grants.location: Online in October 2026, then onsite in Marrakech, Morocco, 22-26 November 2026. Open to Moroccan producers only.
grants.amount: No application fee. Participation in the online and onsite professional programme is covered.
grants.duration: Five-day online programme in October 2026, followed by a five-day onsite programme 22-26 November 2026.
grants.description: Atlas Station is the Marrakech International Film Festival's professional development strand running alongside the Atlas Workshops, aimed at building the Moroccan film industry. The producers track offers structured mentoring, industry sessions and access to the festival's international network during the 9th edition. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: open to Moroccan producers only, not to international applicants. Deadline 31 August 2026. See also the Atlas Station short film track (deadline 14 September 2026) and the internationally open Atlas Workshops track for films in shooting or post-production.

grants.title: Kone Foundation: Annual Grant Call (2026)
grants.location: Finland. Work may be carried out abroad by Finnish citizens. Projects must have a connection to Finland.
grants.amount: Artistic groups and organisations up to EUR 250,000; research groups typically EUR 200,000 to 500,000. Minimum project duration six months for individual applicants and one month for groups; maximum four consecutive years for the same project. No co-financing requirement stated. No application fee. No retroactive funding.
grants.duration: One month to four years; projects must start in January or later.
grants.description: Kone Foundation is Finland's major private funder for academic research in the humanities, social sciences and environmental sciences, for professional artistic work across all disciplines, and specifically for multidisciplinary projects combining scholarly and artistic approaches, which is where digital culture, media arts and artistic research proposals land. Individuals, working groups and legal entities with a Finnish business ID may apply, and artistic groups and organisations can receive up to EUR 250,000. The Finland connection is the binding constraint: a non-Finnish applicant needs a Finnish institutional affiliation, Finland residence, or the work must happen in Finland, though international collaborators can join a group freely once one member is a Finnish citizen or Finland-based. Psychology, theology, law, business studies without an interdisciplinary element, and medical research are not funded, nor are master's studies, continuing education, building renovation, standalone equipment purchases or hobby activity. The annual call runs 1 to 15 September each year, closing 15 September 2026 at 16:00 EEST, with decisions announced in November and December.
