grants.description: The Doc Society Climate Story Fund, run by Doc Society's Climate Story Unit, provides grants of up to USD 125,000 to support non-fiction projects in late production and the implementation of impact campaigns for both completed and in-production projects. The fund supports compelling independent media storytelling and impact strategies aligned with the Fund's mission around climate justice and biodiversity. This call has no set theme, welcoming applications across all areas aligned with the Fund's mission. Since 2021 the fund has distributed more than USD 4M to over 50 projects, with grantee work reaching distribution through outlets including BBC, POV, Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Spotify, YouTube, and WhatsApp. WHAT YOU GET: up to USD 125,000 to support non-fiction projects in late production and impact campaigns. WHO IS ELIGIBLE: open to filmmakers of any nationality. DEADLINE: 24 August 2026. TO APPLY: see the fund page and apply via the Doc Society application. Questions: climate@docsociety.org.

grants.title: National Gallery of Iceland: CUSP Artist Residency (Reykjavik 2027)
grants.organization: National Gallery of Iceland (Listasafn Islands), CUSP project
grants.location: Reykjavik, Iceland. Residency hosted by the National Gallery of Iceland.
grants.amount: Accommodation and working space for the residency; travel and subsistence stipend; an artist fee for collaborating in the open-lab/masterclass; and, depending on the artist's request and museum means, hardware and software for the working space. No application fee.
grants.duration: Up to four weeks, taking place in early 2027, with exact dates arranged with the selected artist.
grants.description: The National Gallery of Iceland announces an artist residency open call under its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe's Culture grant. Artists working in complex media or emerging technologies (e.g. generative AI, custom sensors, sound, software-based, blockchain, physical and digital hybrid) are invited to apply. This is the first of four residency stays offered to different artists through the program, one in each of the participating countries (Iceland, Norway, Czechia, and Ukraine), followed by two micro residencies in the Netherlands and Iceland. The programme brings together artists working in time-based media with museum professionals, conservators, and technology specialists developing preservation and conservation methodologies to ensure the long-term endurance of artworks. The selected artist will meet with a preservation specialist or conservator specializing in time-based media art for an in-depth artist interview addressing the preservation needs of their medium, and will present their body of work and working methods publicly during an open-lab masterclass designed in collaboration with the museum. RESIDENCY: up to four weeks in early 2027 in Reykjavik, exact dates arranged with the selected artist. WHAT IS PROVIDED: accommodation and working space; a travel and subsistence stipend; an artist fee for the open lab/masterclass; and possibly hardware and software depending on the artist's request and museum means. ELIGIBILITY: international artists based outside Iceland; applicants must be residents of any of the 27 EU member states or of non-EU countries with association agreements (EFTA/EEA members, acceding countries, candidate countries, and European Neighbourhood Policy countries). APPLICATION: complete the application form with full name, country of residence, gender identity, contact information, an artistic statement (max 2500 characters), a motivation letter (max 2500 characters), a draft idea of the public workshop or masterclass (max 1000 characters), links to social media/professional websites, and a CV and portfolio upload (max 10MB each). DEADLINE: 3 September 2026 at 23:59 GMT. ABOUT CUSP: Creative Understanding, Saving and Preserving Time-Based Media Art is a transnational cooperation project co-funded by the EU's Creative Europe Culture grant, led by the National Gallery of Iceland with Nasjonalmuseet (Norway), LI-MA (Netherlands), Vasulka Kitchen (Czechia), and Mystetskyi Art Arsenal (Ukraine), focused on preserving and presenting time-based media art. Inquiries: cusp.residency.is [at] gmail.com.

grants.title: Prospect Art: NEW WORK Commission 2027 - "We Come in Pieces"
grants.location: Remote / online. Open to visual artists worldwide; programs (ONE WORK, BROADCAST) run online.
grants.amount: NEW WORK: USD 1,500 commission for one artist, plus a featured website section and social promotion. BROADCAST: USD 125 screening or speaking fee if selected. ONE WORK: a published article (exposure). NOTE: a USD 10 administrative fee applies to apply, with a no-questions-asked waiver available on request before the deadline. PayPal account required to receive funds.
grants.duration: The commissioned NEW WORK project should be completed within twelve months of selection.
grants.description: Prospect Art invites visual artists worldwide to apply for the 2027 NEW WORK commission, a USD 1,500 project grant supporting the creation of a new, conceptually driven work responding to the curatorial theme "We Come in Pieces," developed by 2026-2027 Curatorial Fellow Alma Sammel. Through a single application, artists are also considered for ONE WORK (an online series featuring an in-depth conversation centered on a single completed artwork) and BROADCAST (a curated online program of screenings, artist talks, and discussions). THEME: "We Come in Pieces" proposes the Alien as a method for shifting perspective, approaching alienness as a practice of estrangement to encounter the world beyond familiar human-centered narratives. It explores relationships between human and more-than-human worlds, speculative cosmologies, ecological systems, technologies, landscapes, histories, infrastructures, and nonhuman forms of intelligence (satellites and orbital debris, fungal networks, oceans, atmospheric systems, algorithmic intelligences), inviting works that displace the point of listening, seeing, sensing, or knowing. Research-based and conceptually driven practices are especially encouraged. WHAT'S OFFERED: NEW WORK, USD 1,500 to one artist plus a featured website section and social promotion (project completed within 12 months); ONE WORK, a published article and social promotion; BROADCAST, a USD 125 screening or speaking fee and inclusion in a themed program. ELIGIBILITY: professional visual artists working in any medium at any career stage, except those currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate studio art programs; collectives may apply. Media welcomed include moving image, installation, sculpture, photography, performance, sound, digital media, social practice, and interdisciplinary forms. APPLICATION: submit via the official Google Form with contact information, a project description (250 words), a sketch/visualization (1-3 images), up to 3 links to completed work samples, a statement relating the project to the theme (200 words), a short bio and exhibition history (500 words), and a budget breakdown of the USD 1,500. A USD 10 administrative fee is paid via PayPal (include PayPal name and transaction ID); a fee waiver is available with no explanation by emailing submissions@prospectart.org before the deadline. Writers may email gioj@prospectart.org with samples. DEADLINE: 16 August 2026; results for the NEW WORK grant notified by end of September. INFO SESSION: 5 August 2026 at noon PST.

grants.title: Royal Conservatoire Antwerp: Call for Artistic Research Proposals (2027 start)
grants.organization: Royal Conservatoire Antwerp (AP University of the Arts)
grants.location: Antwerp, Belgium. Salaried research position; international applicants must hold a valid Belgian work permit.
grants.amount: Salaried research position (contractual appointment). Start projects: 20% employment for 12 months + EUR 1,000 operating resources. One-year projects: 55% employment for 12 months + EUR 1,000. Two-year projects: 55% employment for 24 months + EUR 2,000. No application fee.
grants.duration: Projects start at the earliest 20 September 2027. Start and one-year projects run 12 months; two-year projects run 24 months.
grants.description: The Royal Conservatoire Antwerp (AP University of the Arts) invites applications for artistic research projects starting 20 September 2027, in three types: start projects, one-year projects, and two-year research projects. Applications are embedded in one or more of the Conservatoire's four research groups, supervised by a supervisor, and must align with the Conservatoire's mission and vision. FOCAL POINTS across disciplines: research into improvisation and intuitive creation and performance practices; new dramaturgical and scenographic approaches in cross-over projects; methodologies for interdisciplinary creation processes; sustainable relationships between artists and urban communities; the possibilities and limitations of inclusion in education and/or on stage; and well-being and resilience in music and performing arts. FUNDING (salaried research position): start projects, 20% employment for 12 months plus EUR 1,000 operating resources; one-year projects, 55% employment for 12 months plus EUR 1,000; two-year projects, 55% employment for 24 months plus EUR 2,000. PRECONDITIONS: the applicant holds a relevant master's degree and conducts research situated in or arising from their own artistic practice with the capacity for discursivity; the proposal must align with the Conservatoire's mission/vision; the applicant must be able to enter contractual employment with the Royal Conservatoire Antwerp/AP University of the Arts for the duration of the project (international applicants must hold a valid Belgian work permit); proposals may be submitted only in Dutch or English. PROCEDURE (two steps): STEP 1, submit an expression of interest by 21 September 2026, 12:00 noon (applicants informed by the week of 5 October whether they may develop a full proposal with a research group); STEP 2, submit the full project dossier by 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon. Evaluation by an independent reading committee aims to conclude in March 2027. Contact: Kevin Voets, Head of Research, kevin.voets@ap.be.

It is designed to nurture emerging and promising content creators, giving them the opportunity to create content on topics with significant meaning to them while gaining experience with FUJIFILM GFX System gear, including the GFX ETERNA 55 filmmaking camera. Proposed projects may be submitted as still photography or in movie format. AWARDS: both tiers include complimentary use of a GFX System camera body and two GF lenses for the duration of the project, plus mentoring and technical assistance from Fujifilm technicians and product experts. At the end of the production period in May 2027, recipients' final content is showcased on fujifilm-x.com, with a series of exhibitions planned in various countries. ELIGIBILITY: open to both amateur and professional photographers and videographers who are residents of the countries/regions listed in the Entry Submission section of the program page; not open to employees or officers of FUJIFILM and its subsidiaries. TO APPLY: combine three items into a single PDF: (1) the preformatted cover letter (downloadable from the program page); (2) the project proposal covering descriptive plan, objectives, evaluation and outcome measures, communications, how you will use the Fujifilm partnership and mentoring, schedule, and budget; (3) a portfolio for each individual involved. Proposals must be in English (optionally accompanied by a version in your own language; language proficiency is not judged). Entry period 16 June to 17 August 2026.

grants.description: The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology, Williamsport, PA) invites artists to apply for solo, two-person, or group exhibitions for its 2027-28 season. All entries are juried through a blind selection process by a gallery committee of faculty, staff, K-12 art educators, and community artists; review takes place during the Fall semester and artists receive notification in January. PROVIDED: housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend. Promotional support includes an annual gallery catalog, postcards, press releases, and web and social media. THE SPACE: the Gallery is 3,000 square feet with 82-250 running feet of linear wall space and an 11'4" ceiling. All exhibitions are installed by Gallery staff; site-specific installations requiring artist installation need a planning document approved before scheduling. Artists must have enough work for a solo exhibition unless applying for a two-person show. ENGAGEMENT: campus visits are an important part of programming (some exhibitions are scheduled without a visit). Penn College offers a B.S. in Graphic Design with foundation courses in drawing, 2D and 3D design, visual literacy, painting, ceramics, wood sculpture, printmaking, and computer graphics; artists are encouraged to propose class-specific programs and optional community workshops. Visiting artists give a 20-30 minute gallery talk during the public reception (held Tuesdays through Thursdays). TO APPLY: 10-15 digital images of work (JPG/JPEG only, max 4 MB each), an image list with dimensions and medium, a CV, and an artist statement. For two-person or group proposals, provide details in the comments; for video work, upload a PDF with video links and details. Deadline 31 August 2026 for the 2027-28 season.

grants.title: Railyard Art Project: Call for Temporary Public Art (Santa Fe)
grants.location: Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States (Railyard Park + Plaza, City-owned property under a Conservation Easement).
grants.amount: USD 3,500 honorarium per project (two projects selected), plus marketing support and liability insurance. Funded by Santa Fe's Arts and Culture Commission. No application fee.
grants.duration: Two projects hosted between October 2026 and June 2027.
grants.description: The Railyard Art Project (RAP) facilitates temporary public art installations by established and emerging artists and arts collectives in Santa Fe's Railyard Park + Plaza. RAP is accepting proposals for temporary public art installations and creative projects; thanks to funding from Santa Fe's Arts and Culture Commission, two projects will be hosted between October 2026 and June 2027, each receiving a USD 3,500 honorarium plus marketing support and liability insurance. THEMES: the RAP Committee encourages collaboration across disciplines (art, science, history) and welcomes thoughtful, challenging, playful, and edifying art in the context of social and cultural expression and environmental sustainability. Proposed projects must physically withstand outdoor public display and engage the community by responding to the natural and social landscape of the park. SELECTION CRITERIA: overall artistic merit; context and familiarity with the proposed site; practical viability; and potential for community engagement and cultural/educational enrichment. Artists should select an eligible area of the park's open space and describe the project in detail; photos or renderings may be uploaded with the application (a map of Railyard Art Locations is linked from the program page). The RAP Committee, made up of community members and Park + Plaza stakeholders, selects and schedules the exhibitions; a formal in-person presentation may be requested depending on complexity. CONDITIONS: the park operates under a Conservation Easement, so installations cannot be located on planted areas, no staking of any kind is permitted (including during install/de-install), and nothing may be hung from trees. Artists lend artwork at their own risk (no protection against vandalism or weather damage, and artists are responsible for repairs). Installs and de-installs must be coordinated in advance with the RAP Committee or Railyard Park Conservancy staff, with a Committee or staff member on site throughout. Application deadline 5 August 2026.

grants.title: Target Margin Theater: TMT Institute Fellowship 2026-27
grants.location: Brooklyn, New York, United States (Sunset Park). Fellows must be available in person for intensives, monthly breakfasts, and excursions.
grants.amount: USD 2,000 stipend, plus space, material resources, and collaborators to support each Fellow's experiments. No application fee.
grants.duration: 2026-27 season: three intensive sessions in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, 19-21 March 2027), monthly breakfasts October 2026 through May 2027, and an Open Studio weekend in June 2027.
grants.description: Target Margin Theater invites applications for its next cohort of TMT Institute Fellows for the 2026/2027 season. The Institute is a cohort of artists who seek to radically disrupt and re-examine their existing practice without any goal or expected result: pure experimentation with no product-oriented end goal. Fellows pursue no project, no developmental stage, no deliverable; misfires, dead ends, and bad ideas are considered a fruitful part of the work. SUPPORT: TMT provides space, material resources, collaborators, and a USD 2,000 stipend. STRUCTURE: three short intensive sessions at Target Margin Theater in Brooklyn (5-8 November 2026, 8-10 January 2027, and 19-21 March 2027, all day with some evening hours), monthly breakfasts at Junior's in Brooklyn (20 October, 30 November, 4 January, 1 February, 8 March, 5 April, 3 May), and occasional excursions. After the second intensive, each Fellow commits to an exploration pursued outside group gatherings, supported by TMT resources. The season ends with an Open Studio weekend in June 2027 to share explorations with the community; this is not a performance and should not be an audience-attended, time-bounded show. WHO CAN APPLY: artists from any discipline within or outside theater, as well as production, technical, and administrative workers in the arts. Applicants must have an established, existing body of work and practice they are committed to changing; do not apply with a project. Recent graduates of training programs are unlikely to be appropriate candidates; no formal education level or degree is required. SELECTION: TMT staff and artistic community review applications and invite a handful of candidates to interview; all applicants are notified by October. Deadline: Wednesday 22 July 2026, 11:59 pm EST.

grants.title: In Listening 2027: Call for Hybrid Radio/Live Works (CTM Festival, Berlin)
grants.organization: CTM Festival with Deutschlandfunk Kultur and ORF
grants.location: Berlin, Germany. Premiered at CTM 2027 and broadcast on Deutschlandfunk Kultur, with onward presentation via ORF Oe1 (Zeit-Ton or Blaue Stunde / Kunstradio) and/or ORF musikprotokoll im steirischen herbst in Graz. Applications accepted internationally, submitted in English.
grants.amount: Two selected works are each supported by a fee of EUR 6,000. CTM covers travel to Berlin and lodging during the production and festival periods; technical and staging costs for the CTM presentation (and possible ORF musikprotokoll presentation) are covered separately by arrangement. Research, creation and collaborator costs are the artist's own. Radio-production support (translations, voiceovers, studio time) can be provided by Deutschlandfunk Kultur upon discussion. No application fee.
grants.duration: Work premiered at CTM Festival 22-31 January 2027; radio broadcast Spring 2027; ORF/musikprotokoll presentation Autumn 2027. Remote production phase late October 2026 to January 2027.
grants.description: In Listening is the renamed successor to the CTM Radio Lab, after more than a decade of collaboration between CTM Festival and Germany's public radio Deutschlandfunk Kultur, with support from Austria's ORF, zeroing in on sound-focused experiences. This open call is for works strongly grounded in experimental sound practices and audio art and driven by conceptual approaches or sonic narratives, exploring the blurred edges between sound, noise, music, storytelling, poetry, and documenting, where sound is the main medium. Works should respond to the CTM 2027 theme 'Process...ing', with active listening informing the proposals. Applications should describe how the work could be developed for two complementary outputs: a LIVE EVENT at CTM 2027 and a RADIO BROADCAST on Deutschlandfunk Kultur and Oe1/ORF. At CTM, works are presented in the silent green Kuppelhalle with an intimate setup, the audience seated around the performer(s) and surrounded by a 6.1-channel PA (creative use of fewer channels, stereo, or mono is welcome; minimal lighting and scenography or performances in the dark are suitable, but video and complex scenography are out of scope). For radio/podcast, proposals should consider the individual listening experience (a recording of the performance is not sufficient); the broadcast is a 40-55 minute piece aired in a late-night slot to a largely German-speaking, non-specialist audience. Works premiere at CTM 2027 (22-31 January 2027, Berlin), are broadcast in Deutschlandfunk Kultur's Klangkunst programme in Spring 2027, and presented via ORF (Oe1 Zeit-Ton or Blaue Stunde / Kunstradio) and/or ORF musikprotokoll im steirischen herbst in Graz (Autumn 2027), then available for streaming for at least one year. BUDGET: two selected works each receive EUR 6,000; winners give up to two performances at CTM. Group proposals are possible but should keep a modest travel budget. JURY: Jan Rohlf (CTM), Marcus Gammel (Deutschlandfunk Kultur), Anna Soucek (ORF Oe1), and one independent artist. TIMELINE: deadline 6 September 2026 at 23:59 Berlin time; winners announced mid-October 2026; remote production late October 2026 to January 2027. APPLY (in English, PDF, max 20MB) with a project description including rough budget (max 4 pages), technical requirements, and CV; questions to in_listening@ctm-festival.de. No application fee.

grants.description: Hypha etc. hosts a six-week EU-funded residency (1 October to 10 November 2026) in Campu Cetatii, Transylvania, on the theme Night as Commons and the Dark Side of Light: night, darkness, and light pollution, a strong fit for media and installation practices. Support: EUR 30/day allowance, accommodation, travel allowance (EUR 400 under 5,000 km, EUR 800 over), plus green mobility, family, and accessibility top-ups. ELIGIBILITY: artists based in Creative Europe countries except Romania. Deadline 1 August 2026.

grants.title: Fondation Francois Schneider: Contemporary Talents Competition - The Earth
grants.location: Wattwiller, France. Open internationally to professional artists; sculpture and installation only.
grants.amount: EUR 15,000 per laureate (includes acquisition; EUR 8,000 for editioned works), plus exhibition at the foundation. No entry fee.
grants.duration: Call runs June to August 2026; laureates exhibited at the foundation in Wattwiller.
grants.description: The Fondation Francois Schneider's Contemporary Talents competition, themed The Earth for this edition, awards EUR 15,000 per laureate (including acquisition of the work; EUR 8,000 for editioned works) plus an exhibition at the foundation's centre in Wattwiller. ELIGIBILITY: professional artists internationally, in SCULPTURE AND INSTALLATION only (video or digital work alone does not qualify). NOTE: the 23 August 2026 deadline is from a listing site; the organizer page only states the call runs June to August, so verify the exact date before applying.

grants.title: Structurist Creative Research Fellowship (4th round)
grants.organization: University of Saskatchewan Art Galleries and Collection
grants.location: Saskatoon, Canada (travel and accommodation covered for the Saskatoon component). Open internationally, any career stage.
grants.amount: Project budget up to CAD 20,000, plus travel and accommodation for the Saskatoon research component. No application fee.
grants.duration: Research-creation fellowship around The Structurist journal archive.
grants.description: The University of Saskatchewan Art Galleries offer the Structurist Creative Research Fellowship, supporting art-and-science research-creation engaging The Structurist, the art and architecture journal published at the university from 1960 to 2010. The fellowship provides a project budget of up to CAD 20,000 plus travel and accommodation for the Saskatoon component. Open internationally at any career stage. Deadline 31 August 2026.

grants.title: KHN Center for the Arts: Artist Residency
grants.organization: Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts
grants.location: Nebraska City, Nebraska, United States. Open internationally.
grants.amount: USD 175/week stipend, plus free living and studio space. $35 application fee, collected via the SlideRoom application portal.
grants.duration: Residencies of 2-8 weeks; applications reviewed in two annual cycles (1 March and 1 September). The 2027 1st Session covers awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027.
grants.description: The Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts (KHN) in Nebraska City supports established and emerging writers, visual artists, and composers/musicians by providing living and studio space that allows uninterrupted time for work, reflection, and creative growth. Residencies run 2 to 8 weeks and include free living and studio space plus a USD 175/week stipend. KHN awards approximately 30-38 residencies per session, of which roughly 8-12 go to visual artists working in various media. Categories: Writers & Poets, Visual Artists, Composers & Musicians, and Interdisciplinary Artists. Visual artists work in one of three studios (two approximately 425 sq ft and one 258 sq ft) outfitted with work tables, running water, and storage shelves; donated hand tools, a bandsaw, miter saw, and painting easels are available. Upon request, artists with previous printing experience may access the onsite Harry Duncan Letterpress Studio (SP15 Vandercook Proof Press, a 16x12 inch boxcar base for adhesive plates, furniture, fonts, and a small inventory of printmaking tools). Open internationally. Applications are reviewed twice a year (deadlines 1 March and 1 September); the 2027 1st Session (deadline 1 September 2026) is for awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027. All applications must be submitted online via SlideRoom; mailed or emailed applications are not considered. A $35 application fee is collected through the portal.

grants.title: Hiding in Plain Site: International Public Art Short Film Festival
grants.location: United States / online; screenings sited in public space. Open internationally.
grants.amount: Screening; selected filmmakers receive a modest stipend (amount to be confirmed, revenue-dependent). Free to submit.
grants.duration: Short films 2-20 minutes; festival screens work in public sites.
grants.description: Hiding in Plain Site is an international public art short film festival accepting film, video art, XR, and explicitly AI-generated or AI-assisted moving image works of 2 to 20 minutes, screened in public space. Free to submit; selected filmmakers receive a modest stipend whose amount is revenue-dependent and not yet confirmed. Deadline 10 September 2026.

grants.title: THE ONE International Digital Art Biennial (3rd edition)
grants.location: Torun and Wloclawek, Poland. Open internationally; works may NOT be AI-generated.
grants.amount: Prizes PLN 3,000 / 2,000 / 1,000, plus exhibition and an ISBN catalog. Free entry.
grants.duration: Biennial exhibition in Torun and Wloclawek.
grants.description: THE ONE International Digital Art Biennial, organized by Pinata Group in Torun and Wloclawek, Poland, accepts digital art internationally with free entry; prizes are PLN 3,000, 2,000, and 1,000, plus exhibition and an ISBN catalog. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: submitted works may not be AI-generated. NOTE: the 15 September 2026 deadline is from a listing site and is not stated on the organizer page; verify before submitting.

grants.title: Columbia Institute for Ideas and Imagination: Paris Fellowship 2027-28
grants.organization: Columbia University Institute for Ideas and Imagination
grants.location: Paris, France (Reid Hall). Any nationality; artists must NOT be permanently resident in the United States.
grants.amount: USD 75,000 stipend, plus housing at Reid Hall in Paris and office and research support, September 2027 to May 2028. No application fee.
grants.duration: Fellowship year September 2027 to May 2028 at Reid Hall, Paris.
grants.description: Columbia University's Institute for Ideas and Imagination brings a cohort of scholars and artists to Reid Hall in Paris for an academic year (September 2027 to May 2028), with a USD 75,000 stipend, housing, and research support. The creative-arts category explicitly includes visual and sound arts and film alongside writing and composition. ELIGIBILITY: any nationality, but artists must not be permanently residentent in the United States (Netherlands-based artists qualify). Deadline 30 September 2026.

grants.title: European Cultural Foundation: Artistic Research Fellowship (ECF Historical Archives)
grants.location: Archives held at the Historical Archives of the European Union, Florence, Italy. Open to artists able to work with the archives.
grants.amount: EUR 10,000 artistic-research grant covering travel, accommodation, and living costs; output delivered within 2 years. No application fee.
grants.duration: Research fellowship in the ECF historical archives; output within two years.
grants.description: The European Cultural Foundation invites artists to research its historical archives, held at the Historical Archives of the European Union in Florence, through a new Artistic Research Fellowship with a EUR 10,000 grant covering travel, accommodation, and living costs; the artistic output is delivered within two years. A strong fit for archive-driven, research-based, and critical data practices. Deadline 30 September 2026, 17:00 CET. ELIGIBILITY: professional creatives in visual arts, performing arts, film and audiovisual practices, podcasting and audio storytelling, documentary, journalism or literary practices, who can demonstrate a research-based practice and a clear dissemination strategy. Applications and all supporting documentation must be in English, submitted via the online form. Fellows work at the HAEU inside the scholarly community of the European University Institute, with the archives housed at Villa Salviati. A parallel Academic Research Fellowship of EUR 5,000, for PhD and postdoctoral researchers, early-career researchers within ten years of their master's or doctorate, and independent scholars, is listed separately on the desk and shares this deadline.

grants.title: Fonds 21: Kunst & Cultuur Project Grants (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: Netherlands. Dutch foundations, associations and non-profit BVs/NVs; projects must reach a broad and/or new audience in the Netherlands.
grants.amount: Minimum request EUR 10,000, no stated maximum; around EUR 11.5 million awarded per year across all pillars. No application fee.
grants.duration: Project funding; apply at least four months before the project starts.
grants.description: Fonds 21 supports professional, high-quality art and culture projects by Dutch non-profit organizations (foundations, associations and non-profit BVs/NVs), across performing arts, visual arts, film, literature and interdisciplinary work, with additional pillars for arts education and youth & society. The minimum request is EUR 10,000 with no stated maximum, and roughly EUR 11.5 million is available annually. Applications are accepted year-round via the online portal (after a short eligibility snelcheck) and must be submitted at least four months before the project start date. Free-of-charge events are generally not supported; the fund expects most programming to be paid-access. No application fee.

grants.title: Het Cultuurfonds: Project Grants for Foundations and Associations (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: Netherlands. National office plus provincial chapters; projects in culture, nature and science.
grants.amount: Typically EUR 15,000 to EUR 50,000 for national project applications by foundations and associations; smaller amounts via provincial chapters and themed funds (EUR 1,500 to EUR 25,000). Individual makers and collectives can request up to EUR 5,000. No application fee.
grants.duration: Project funding; decision within roughly 2 weeks to 3 months depending on the route.
grants.description: Het Cultuurfonds (formerly Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds) invests over EUR 40 million per year in culture and nature in the Netherlands. Foundations and associations can apply year-round for project grants (typically EUR 15,000 to EUR 50,000 at national level), and since 2025 individual makers and collectives can apply for up to EUR 5,000. Provincial chapters run their own quarterly rounds for regional projects, and numerous themed funds (EUR 5,000 to EUR 25,000) cover specific disciplines. Rolling intake via the online application portal. No application fee.

grants.title: VSBfonds: Kunst & Cultuur Donations (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: European Netherlands. Private legal entities (foundations, associations); applicants without a registered legal form are also eligible.
grants.amount: No fixed minimum or maximum; the requested amount must be in proportion to other funding sources. No application fee.
grants.duration: Project funding; apply at least four months before the start date (two months for amateur arts initiatives).
grants.description: VSBfonds supports cultural initiatives that make it possible for everyone in the Netherlands to take part in art and culture, spanning ten programme lines from professional performances to community arts. Applications are accepted year-round with no deadlines from foundations, associations and applicants without a formal legal form, and must be submitted at least four months before the initiative starts (two months for amateur arts). A two-minute online quickscan checks eligibility before the formal application. No fixed minimum or maximum amount; the request should be proportionate to other funding. No application fee.

grants.title: SIDN fonds: Pioneer Projects for a Strong Internet (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: Netherlands. Open to natural persons and legal entities for the pioneer track; theme calls require legal entities.
grants.amount: Up to EUR 10,000 per pioneer project; theme calls (once or twice a year) fund larger projects above EUR 10,000. No application fee.
grants.duration: Pioneer projects develop an idea into a demo, pilot or experimental design; continuous intake.
grants.description: SIDN fonds (the foundation behind the .nl domain registry) invests in daring projects with societal added value that contribute to a strong internet and strong internet users. The Pioneers track is continuously open and awards up to EUR 10,000 to develop an innovative idea into a demo, pilot or experimental design; it is open to both individuals and legal entities. Larger projects are funded through theme calls issued once or twice a year (legal entities only). Projects must show innovation and public value and share their results openly; plain website or app building and purely B2B proposals are excluded. No application fee.

grants.title: Stichting DOEN: Funding for Pioneering Culture and Social Initiatives (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: Netherlands-based fund (backed by the Dutch charity lotteries); themes have differing geographic focus areas. Legal entities only.
grants.amount: No fixed amounts published; funding is tailored per initiative. No application fee.
grants.duration: Apply at least four months before the project start date; the application procedure takes about four months.
grants.description: Stichting DOEN, funded by the Dutch charity lotteries, supports pioneering initiatives within themes including the transformative power of imagination (art and culture), regenerative economy and solidarity economy. Applications are accepted year-round via the Mijn DOEN portal from legal entities only (no individuals) and must be received at least four months before the project starts; the assessment procedure takes about four months. Amateur art practice and standalone productions of films, books, CDs or websites are not supported. No application fee.

grants.title: Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie: Open Schemes for Cultural Institutions 2025-2028 (rolling, Netherlands)
grants.location: Netherlands and the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. Cultural institutions, vocational education institutions and interdisciplinary makers.
grants.amount: EUR 5,000 to EUR 75,000 depending on the scheme (e.g. cultural education in mbo EUR 5,000-55,000, in vmbo/vso/pro EUR 10,000-65,000, design-based learning platforms up to EUR 75,000, interdisciplinary makers EUR 12,500-50,000). No application fee.
grants.duration: Schemes run within the 2025-2028 policy period; multiple schemes currently open.
grants.description: The Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie, one of the Dutch national cultural funds (annual budget around EUR 30 million), currently has several schemes open for applications: cultural education in vocational education (mbo, EUR 5,000-55,000), cultural education in vmbo/vso/pro (EUR 10,000-65,000), cultural education for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (EUR 5,000-50,000), an open call for design-based learning platforms (up to EUR 75,000) and an interdisciplinary scheme for professional makers (EUR 12,500-50,000). Most schemes target cultural institutions, in some cases in partnership with schools. See the subsidies overview for per-scheme conditions. No application fee.

grants.title: Woodward/Newman Award 2027-28 (Constellation Stage & Screen)
grants.location: Bloomington, Indiana, USA. Open submissions of unpublished plays; production takes place in Bloomington.
grants.amount: USD 3,000 cash prize (in lieu of royalties) plus a full production in Constellation's Mainstage season; housing and transportation provided. No submission fee.
grants.duration: Winner announced by 15 May 2027; production in the 2027-28 season. Submissions stay on file and under consideration for two years.
grants.description: The Woodward/Newman Award, started with the support of Joanne Woodward, Newman's Own Foundation and the Newman family, is awarded annually by Constellation Stage & Screen to the best unpublished new play. The winner receives a USD 3,000 cash prize (in lieu of royalties) and a full production in the Mainstage season, with housing and transportation provided. The contest format and submission fees have been eliminated: submissions are reviewed on an ongoing basis and are also considered for all seven production slots in the season, including TYA (theatre for young audiences) shows. Full-length plays should run 75 to 135 minutes; TYA shows over 40 minutes. Plays must be unpublished at submission (independently published is acceptable); limit of two submissions per playwright per year; musicals may include demos. Plays submitted by midnight 31 August 2026 are considered for the 2027-28 season; later submissions roll to 2028-29. All submissions are kept on file for two years.

grants.title: Medialab Matadero: Situated Research Residencies 2027 (Madrid)
grants.location: Madrid, Spain. In-person residency; open internationally to individuals and collectives.
grants.amount: EUR 10,000 per project (before taxes) for three selected projects, plus individual workspace, Fablab and technical materials, curatorial guidance, and logistical and financial support for public activities. No application fee.
grants.duration: January to July 2027; cannot be carried out remotely, with extended stays in Madrid recommended especially March to June. Live online Q&A on 8 September 2026, 6pm CEST.
grants.description: Medialab Matadero in Madrid selects three projects for a research and creation residency bringing together contemporary art, design, science, technology and society, welcoming critical, experimental and collaborative work. Each project must connect clearly with one or more themes from Medialab's recent programs: LAB 1 Sentient Media, LAB 2 The Metabolic Sublime, LAB 3 Synthetic Minds, LAB 4 Weird Futures and LAB 5 The Mechanics of Truth. Open to individuals and collectives from any discipline (design, art, architecture, film, journalism, digital media, environmental science, philosophy, engineering, programming, activism and more). SUPPORT: EUR 10,000 per project (before taxes), individual workspace, access to the Fablab and technical materials, curatorial team guidance, and logistical and financial support for public activities; proposals must include public engagement plans and produce documentation. RESIDENCY: January to July 2027, in person in Madrid. DEADLINE: 27 September 2026. No application fee.

grants.title: Flickr x Black Women Photographers Grant 2026 (Traces of Connection)
grants.location: Open internationally to Black female and non-binary photographers; winner announced at the MODE by Flickr festival in Minneapolis, USA (18-20 September 2026).
grants.amount: USD 10,000 grant to invest in the recipient's practice, plus a two-year Flickr Pro and one-year SmugMug Pro membership; ten additional recipients each receive one-year Flickr Pro and SmugMug Pro memberships. No entry fee (BWP membership is free).
grants.duration: Winner announced live at MODE by Flickr, 18-20 September 2026
grants.description: Flickr and Black Women Photographers award a USD 10,000 grant to a Black female or non-binary photographer to invest in their practice. The 2026 edition centers on the theme Traces of Connection, chosen by 2025 recipient and guest judge Eleonore Menga. TO APPLY: be a member of the Black Women Photographers organization (free), join the BWP Flickr Community, submit one photograph inspired by the theme to the community, and share a brief description of how the image connects to it. The winner also receives a two-year Flickr Pro and a one-year SmugMug Pro membership, and is announced live at the first MODE by Flickr festival in Minneapolis (18-20 September 2026); ten additional recipients receive Flickr Pro and SmugMug Pro memberships. DEADLINE: 6 August 2026. No entry fee.

grants.title: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation: Book Grants (Public Understanding of Science and Technology)
grants.location: Remote / anywhere (US foundation; grants paid directly to authors or via a nonprofit host)
grants.amount: Typically up to $60,000 per book grant
grants.duration: Project-based (book research and writing)
grants.description: The one Sloan program that funds individuals directly: grants for authors researching and writing nonfiction books that bring science and technology to a general audience. Over 200 authors supported since 1996. Favoured topics include elucidating confusing or controversial scientific subjects, profiles of figures in science and technology, science-technology-art connections, women and science, and the culture and philosophy of science. Start with a letter of inquiry to program director Doron Weber; full proposals are by invitation only. Reviewed three times a year: LOIs by 1 September (decision by 15 February), 1 January (by 31 May) and 1 May (by 31 October). No application fee.

grants.title: Alicia Patterson Fellowship 2027 (Fund for Investigative Journalism)
grants.organization: Fund for Investigative Journalism (Alicia Patterson Foundation program)
grants.location: Remote; fellows may live anywhere, but projects must be U.S.-focused for publication in American outlets
grants.amount: $40,000 (12-month fellowship) or $20,000 (6-month fellowship), paid monthly; covers living and reporting costs
grants.duration: 6 or 12 months, beginning early 2027
grants.description: Long-running fellowship for in-depth, investigative written reporting on subjects of public interest, now administered by the Fund for Investigative Journalism after the foundation's December 2025 merger. For seasoned reporters with a body of in-depth written work; freelancers are encouraged and staff journalists may apply if they take leave (part-time work is allowed during the fellowship, full-time is not). Twelve-month fellows produce four articles, six-month fellows two. Decisions by end of 2026. Distinct from FIJ's regular reporting grants. No application fee.

grants.title: Leon Levy Center for Biography Fellowships 2027-28 (incl. Levy/Sloan Science Biography)
grants.organization: Leon Levy Center for Biography, CUNY Graduate Center
grants.location: New York City, USA (in residence at the CUNY Graduate Center, September to May)
grants.amount: $72,000 stipend plus writing space, full research facilities and research assistance
grants.duration: September 2027 to May 2028 (academic year in residence)
grants.description: Four resident biography fellowships plus the Levy/Sloan Fellowship, funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, for a biography of a figure in science or technology; separate Sherwin fellowship for nuclear-age history. Open to writers of all nationalities, with explicit preference for first-time biographers who have not yet held a biography fellowship, though mid-career and senior writers are welcome; independent writers eligible. Fellows join monthly seminars and the center's public events. Apply with CV, career narrative, project description, writing sample and two references (agents, editors and publishers are discouraged as referees). No application fee.

grants.title: RTM Pitch 2026 (IFFR)
grants.location: Rotterdam, Netherlands
grants.amount: EUR 25,000 for the winner (EUR 20,000 from the City of Rotterdam, EUR 5,000 from VEVAM Fonds) to realise the film, plus tailored coaching and an IFFR premiere; a runner-up receives a EUR 5,000 development budget co-funded by QISSA. No application fee.
grants.duration: Short film of 5 to 20 minutes; winning film premieres during RTM Day at IFFR 2028
grants.description: Eighth edition of RTM Pitch, IFFR's open call for Rotterdam film talent. Submit a plan for a film between 5 and 20 minutes long; a jury of film experts and IFFR programmers selects one filmmaker to receive EUR 25,000 to realise the film (with coaching and an IFFR 2028 premiere) and a runner-up to receive a EUR 5,000 development budget co-funded by QISSA. All filmmakers are welcome; this edition especially encourages genre films (horror, science fiction, thriller, fantasy) that use genre conventions for a distinctive personal vision. Submit a written film plan (story, setting, team, budget and financing, cinematography vision, with optional supporting material) or a video pitch of no more than three minutes (Vimeo or YouTube link) via the application form. Deadline: Sunday 30 August 2026, 23:59 CEST.

grants.title: Adrianna Newell Fellowship at Arts&Rec 2026
grants.location: Stamford, NY (Western Catskills), USA
grants.amount: Live/work residency: use of a 1000 sq ft studio and attached apartment, plus a $1,500 total materials stipend and per diem. Travel (especially international) is not funded. No application fee.
grants.duration: October 2026 (four weeks to two months, based on project needs; possible extension into November)
grants.description: Inaugural Adrianna Newell Fellowship, a live/work studio residency in Stamford, NY (Western Catskills) for October 2026, with possible extension into November. Named for board member Adrianna Newell, it invites queer lens-based artists working in photography and moving image with an active, research-driven or conceptually rich practice, especially work engaging queer perspectives on land, rurality and regional space, or queer identity, memory, intimacy, community and embodiment. Open to artists from everywhere. Fellows receive a 1000 sq ft studio with attached apartment, a $1,500 combined materials stipend and per diem, and introductions to the local creative community; an open-studio presentation, artist talk or public exhibition at the end is required. Travel, especially international, is not funded (residents are encouraged to seek travel support elsewhere). Apply by emailing a single PDF (one-page description of your work and planned project, 10 to 20 work samples with short descriptions, and a current CV) to programs@artsrec.org. Deadline: 31 July 2026; notices by end of August.

grants.title: ZAMEK Artist Residency 2027 (ZAMEK Culture Centre, Poznan)
grants.location: Poznan, Poland
grants.amount: Accommodation in an apartment in the former imperial residence, studio access, a fee of PLN 6,000 gross per month (contract for specific work), a production budget of PLN 5,000 to 15,000 gross depending on length of stay and project, plus curatorial support and publicity. No application fee listed.
grants.duration: 4 to 8 weeks during 2027 (Conceptual or Operational Residency format)
grants.description: Open call for ZAMEK Culture Centre's 2027 Artist-in-Residence programme in Poznan. Supports artists working across visual arts, performance, choreography, dance, music, sound art, architecture and filmmaking (literature is excluded). Two formats: a Conceptual Residency (creative stay, no requirement to complete or present a final work, with public meetings at least every two weeks) and an Operational Residency (concluding with an artistic event such as an exhibition, concert or screening, plus regular public meetings). Selected artists receive accommodation in the former imperial residence, a studio, a fee of PLN 6,000 gross per month, a production budget of PLN 5,000 to 15,000 gross, curatorial support and publicity. Residencies run 4 to 8 weeks in 2027. ZAMEK is particularly interested in projects that engage changing realities, the current moment and the future (climate and migration crises, the war in Ukraine, social and political issues) or the context, history and architecture of the Castle; project scale must fit the programme budget, and projects should not rely on external co-financing. Download the Terms & Conditions on the ZAMEK site to apply. Deadline: 27 July 2026.

grants.title: Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation: Performance Grant (Summer 2026)
grants.location: New York City (five boroughs), or a location in close proximity to NYC approved by the foundation, USA
grants.amount: Up to $10,000 for production costs (performers, collaborators, rehearsal and venue rental, design elements, technical staff, etc.). Does not fund the creation or composition of new work. No application fee.
grants.duration: Production grant; performance must start no sooner than 1 November 2026 and complete by 22 September 2027
grants.description: The Cafe Royal Cultural Foundation NYC Performance Grant supports individual artists producing theatre, dance and performance art (which may be accompanied by music) moving toward a public performance. The Summer 2026 cycle offers up to $10,000 for eligible production costs: actors, dancers and guest performers, director/choreographer/composer and creative-team fees, costumes, lighting, sound, scenic, props and set, rehearsal and venue rental, and production and technical staff. Funds do not cover the creation or composition of new work; if the performance is a play it must be a full production (readings do not qualify). ELIGIBILITY: individual performers only (not groups or organizations) who are US citizens or resident aliens, current NYC residents who have lived in the city at least one year and will remain through project completion. This cycle accepts only 40 applications and closes early if that cap is reached. Applicants may submit up to 5 video links. Apply via the foundation's performance page. Deadline: 3 August 2026, 9:00 am ET (or earlier if 40 applications are received).

grants.title: Digital Cultures Festival 2026: Best of Poland Open Call
grants.organization: Digital Cultures Festival (Monster Mind Studio); Pitch Award funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute
grants.location: Warsaw, Poland (live pitches on 24 September 2026)
grants.amount: Best of Poland Pitch Award: a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 (funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute) for the jury's top pick, to support participation in a European industry event. Up to 10 creators also receive pitch coaching and expert feedback. No application fee.
grants.duration: Live 7-minute pitch showcase on 24 September 2026
grants.description: Best of Poland is the Digital Cultures Festival's showcase for work at the intersection of art and technology. Open to anyone working creatively in digital media (artists, filmmakers, game developers, UX designers, programmers, curators, students and more) with projects that show how technology fosters genuine human connection and addresses contemporary social change. Eligible formats include VR, AR, interactive film, games, net art and cross-media works; both completed and in-progress projects qualify. Selected creators present 7-minute live pitches on 24 September 2026 in Warsaw; the jury's top pick receives the Best of Poland Pitch Award, a career development grant of up to PLN 5,000 funded by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute to support participation in a European industry event, and up to 10 creators receive pitch coaching with festival director Anna Szylar and expert feedback. Free to apply via the form on the festival site. Deadline: 1 August 2026.

grants.title: APOSTAXIS Artist Residency & Exhibition 2026 (Ukraine / Cyprus)
grants.location: Ternopil, Ukraine and Larnaca, Cyprus (hybrid participation possible)
grants.amount: Fully funded: artist fee of EUR 1,800 (including tax; paid in equivalent UAH for Ukrainian artists), EUR 300 production budget, plus travel, accommodation, meals and curatorial support. No application fee.
grants.duration: 20-day residency, 6 to 28 October 2026, with a group exhibition in Larnaca in January 2027
grants.description: APOSTAXIS is an international residency and exhibition programme exploring displacement, memory, identity and cultural resilience. It selects four visual artists (three from Ukraine and one from Cyprus) for two simultaneous 20-day residencies in Ternopil, Ukraine and Larnaca, Cyprus (6 to 28 October 2026), followed by post-production, a digital exhibition, and a curated physical exhibition in Larnaca in January 2027. ELIGIBILITY: visual artists from Ukraine and Cyprus with lived experience or family heritage connected to displacement, working in community-engaged or research-based practices (installation, mixed media, participatory, social practice, documentary, performance, archive-based work). Artists unable to travel due to war-related restrictions or personal circumstances remain eligible via hybrid participation. Fully funded: EUR 1,800 artist fee (equivalent UAH for Ukrainian artists), EUR 300 production budget, travel, accommodation, meals and curatorial support; no application fee. Deadline: 26 July 2026.

grants.title: Pandora Short Film Grant 2026
grants.location: United States (early-career US filmmakers)
grants.amount: $12,000 production grant to the winner, plus a Panavision camera package (worth about $15,000), an optional $1,000 Kodak Film Grant toward film stock and lab expenses, mentorship from an award-winning filmmaker, and fiscal sponsorship. Three finalists receive mentorship, fiscal sponsorship, consideration for the Panavision New Filmmaker Program, and $500 off Athos production insurance. ENTRY FEE: tiered, $30 regular ($27 Gold members) and $40 late ($36); Pandora states fee waivers are available on request.
grants.duration: Production grant for a narrative short film (script stage or finishing funds)
grants.description: The Pandora Short Film Grant is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that awards an annual $12,000 grant to an early-career US filmmaker for the production of a narrative short film. Projects at script stage or already filmed and seeking finishing funds are both eligible. The winner also receives a Panavision camera package (about $15,000), an optional $1,000 Kodak Film Grant, mentorship from an award-winning filmmaker (2026 mentors include Alma Har'el, Lila Neugebauer, Lauren Wolkstein, Sarah Elizabeth Mintz and Chris Merola), and fiscal sponsorship; three finalists receive mentorship, fiscal sponsorship, Panavision New Filmmaker Program consideration and discounted production insurance. ELIGIBILITY: open to all early-career US filmmakers; applicants are asked NOT to apply if they have directed a feature film with a budget over $250K or directed or produced television. Selection is blind, based on script and pitch materials, weighting artistic vision over industry resume. TIMELINE: submissions open 30 May 2026, close 1 October 2026, notifications 15 November 2026.

grants.title: transmediale x Pro Helvetia Digital Art Residency 2027

grants.title: Good Life Residents Program: AI and Finance
grants.organization: Roosevelt Institute, in partnership with Data & Society
grants.location: Remote. Travel may be requested for select convenings and for the culminating public event. US economic policy focus.
grants.amount: USD 3,000 stipend, plus travel and accommodation for the culminating event if needed. No application fee.
grants.duration: 6 months, part-time at roughly 5 to 8 hours per month
grants.description: The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month Roosevelt Institute initiative that develops new leaders and elevates bold ideas across six economic policy priorities under its Good Life Agenda. Each topic area hosts a cohort of 3 to 4 residents plus 1 to 2 senior Topic Advisors (academics, policy leaders, organizers or government practitioners) who provide strategic and intellectual mentorship and moderate the closing event. Residents write a roughly 1,500-word original policy essay advancing a people-centered policy vision against a topic-specific prompt, take part in structured dialogue with peers, Topic Advisors and Roosevelt Think Tank directors, help prepare and appear at a culminating public event, contribute to press opportunities such as op-eds and reporter calls where applicable, and act as ambassadors for the Good Life Agenda in their professional and public networks. The current round, the AI and Finance Residents Program, is run in partnership with Data & Society and asks for bold ideas on how to shape, redirect, interrupt or make more visible and contestable the flows of capital into generative AI. Framing: breakneck investment in generative AI technology and infrastructure is distorting the stock market, profit measures, bond issuance, the pace and composition of growth, job creation and trade policy, with seven tech companies accounting for more than a third of S&P 500 market capitalisation and complex, sometimes circular financial arrangements obscuring risk. Suggested lines of inquiry include what government interventions could improve public oversight, risk allocation and direction-setting in private markets; how other investments could be coordinated and scaled if AI spending is crowding them out; what role public spending or new institutions could play in catalysing technology R&D designed to support workers, sustainability and supply chains; what democratic input mechanisms would keep state influence over capital flows less vulnerable to corruption; and how federal AI policy should address public hostility to data centre investments alongside national security and competitiveness. Compensation is USD 3,000 plus travel and accommodation for the culminating event. FLAG: Roosevelt does not publish an application deadline for the AI and Finance round on the programme page, and earlier rounds (Social Security financing, Federal Reserve powers, housing) each ran their own short application window. Check the Formstack application form linked from the programme page for the current closing date before applying.

grants.title: Senior Researcher, AI Civics
grants.location: Fully remote within the United States. Data & Society is based in New York City and operates as a remote-first organisation; occasional onsite meetings possible. You must be living and authorised to work in the US; no visa sponsorship.
grants.amount: USD 78,000 to 97,000 annual salary, commensurate with experience, plus medical, dental and vision insurance, opt-in insurance and 401k products, paid time off and paid federal holidays. No application fee.
grants.duration: Two-year full-time position, September 2026 to 31 May 2028, with no expectation of extension
grants.description: Data & Society, the independent nonprofit studying the social implications of data-centric technologies and automation, is hiring a Senior Researcher for AI Civics, a newly launched two-year programme on civic action and community control over AI. The programme aims to amplify the tools of civic participation so the public can directly shape the role AI plays in society, surfacing civic tools people can use to exert political power over AI systems and tech platforms at community level. It co-creates toolkits and training resources with anchor partner organisations, diffuses them through a train-the-trainer model, and builds toward a national civic coalition demanding democratic accountability over AI. The Senior Researcher is a subject-matter expert and lead contributor, drawing primarily on participatory methods and especially participatory action research, and is responsible for one or more inter-organisational partnerships with national partner organisations working in K-12 education, labour, faith or advocacy. Responsibilities span cultivating and stewarding relationships with partner staff, community members and leaders and public sector workers; leading collaborative relationships with an anchor partner and its local members for the co-creation and diffusion of AI Civics resources; co-developing and iterating toolkits, facilitation guides and training curricula and running piloting, feedback and revision cycles; producing case studies, educational materials, templates, reports, academic publications, lectures and public writing; supporting facilitation preparation for co-design workshops, train-the-trainer sessions and participatory research activities; developing research questions, strategies and new external partnerships with the Program Director; network communications; participating in fundraising, including grant applications and materials for the Development Team; and contributing to the intellectual life of the organisation. REQUIRED: graduate degree or equivalent; expertise in one or more sectors of interest to the programme (K-12 education, labour, faith groups, or another institutional pillar of civic life as it relates to data-centric technologies and AI); 7 to 10 years minimum experience in research organisations or research environments (university, public policy, advocacy, government), inclusive of graduate work; expertise in participatory research methods; a strong track record of seeing research through to publication; a public profile and ability to reach non-academic audiences through writing and speaking; and the ability to coordinate and conduct in-depth qualitative research. PREFERRED: doctoral degree in information science, education, social sciences or similar; established relationships with relevant organisations in the programme themes; experience with civic engagement or organising in nonprofit, labour, advocacy, research or public interest technology contexts. Reports to the Program Director. Data & Society requires prospective employees to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19. TO APPLY: submit a cover letter, an academic CV, and the names, affiliations, titles, email addresses and phone numbers for three references by 30 July 2026. Applications are reviewed from 31 July 2026. Questions: jobs@datasociety.net. NOTE: this is a salaried job, not a grant or fellowship.

grants.title: Luminos.AI Legal Engineering Fellowship (Fall 2026)
grants.location: Remote
grants.amount: USD 35 per hour, part-time. No application fee.
grants.duration: Part-time, flexible 3 to 6 month term
grants.description: Luminos.AI, an embedded AI-governance and legal-risk infrastructure company (built by former Fortune 500 AI governance leads and company-builders), runs a part-time fellowship for a technically inclined law student or recent graduate who wants to work at the frontier of AI agent oversight and risk evaluation. Fellows work directly with senior lawyers and engineers on the practical problem of how to test, evaluate and govern generative and agentic AI systems that change every quarter. WHAT YOU DO: research and help design rigorous testing and evaluation approaches for generative and agentic AI, translating fast-moving legal and regulatory requirements into concrete, testable standards; track the global AI regulatory landscape in real time and turn it into practical guardrails; draft frameworks, workflows and risk assessments that hold up under real deployment conditions; and partner closely with the technical team, where comfort around code, models or data is an asset. Fellows with technical skills who want to spend part of their time working directly with engineering are encouraged to do so. WHO YOU ARE: currently pursuing a JD (or a recent graduate) from a top law program; an excellent researcher and writer comfortable applying existing law to genuinely new situations; genuinely enthusiastic about AI and willing to learn the technical details. Bonus: coding ability, ML/GenAI exposure, or a background in privacy, security or data governance law. TERMS: USD 35 per hour, remote, part-time, flexible 3 to 6 month term, with direct mentorship from senior legal and technical leadership. TO APPLY: send a cover letter, resume, transcript and writing sample to careers@luminos.ai with the subject line 'Application for Luminos.AI Fall 2026 Fellowship'. Rolling review with remote interviews.

grants.title: Law & AI Academic Fellowship
grants.location: Washington DC, USA; Cambridge, UK; or remote
grants.amount: USD 130,000 annual salary. No application fee.
grants.duration: Two years, full-time
grants.description: The Institute for Law & AI (LawAI), an independent think tank researching and advising on the legal challenges posed by artificial intelligence, is running its inaugural Law & AI Academic Fellowship for aspiring legal scholars who intend to go on the US legal academic job market. The fellowship is designed as an alternative to university-sponsored Visiting Assistant Professor or law fellow positions: fellows spend the majority of their time researching and writing articles for publication in law journals on the law of transformative AI, and are prepared for the academic job market as part of a larger application package. Teaching is not required, which LawAI frames as a benefit over most university-affiliated positions, though fellows who want teaching experience are encouraged to seek it and LawAI and its affiliates may be able to help secure positions. Each fellow is paired with an academic mentor from LawAI's network of affiliated academics for ongoing support, with more intensive help in the final stages of the job application process including moot interviews and detailed feedback. Fellows may also inquire about spending time in residence at academic institutions of interest. Candidates are selected in part on how well their research interests align with LawAI's: the institute expects AI to reshape culture, the economy, public policy, public administration, politics, military affairs and geostrategy at least as profoundly as the Industrial Revolution, and asks whether a candidate's research is well-scoped to changes of that magnitude. Areas of particular interest include risk regulation of transformative AI, liability for AI harms, AI and biosecurity, AI and cybersecurity, executive branch use of transformative AI, national security law, law and AI infrastructure, administrative law, constitutional law, international regulation, AI in the judiciary, and industrial policy. Full-time two-year role at USD 130,000 per year, based in Washington DC, Cambridge UK, or remote. Applications close 31 July 2026.

grants.title: Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) Fellowship
